semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ}: There are three views on it, the clearest of which is that it is an adverbial (ẓarf) whose governing verb is omitted, its implied form being: "and remember your condition, firmly established at the time of your fewness." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The second is that it is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is accusative as an explicitly mentioned direct object, not as an adverbial; that is: remember the time of your being few and abased." There is room for objection in this, because «إذ» is not used freely (as a noun) except in the ways I mentioned earlier, and this is not one of them. The third is that it is an adverbial of «اذكروا». Al-Ḥūfī said this, and it is invalid, because the governing word is future while the adverbial is past, so how could the two meet?
His saying: {تَخَافُونَ}: There are three views on it, the most apparent being that it is a third khabar (predicate). The second is that it is an adjective (ṣifa) of «قليل»; the description has begun with the singular and then moved to the sentence. The third is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «مُسْتَضْعَفُون».

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وتخونوا}: It may be accusative by an implied «أَنْ» as the answer to a prohibition, that is: "do not combine the two offences," as in his saying:
2404 - لا تَنْهَ عن خُلُقٍ وتأتيَ مثلَه ... عارٌ عليك إذا فَعَلْت عظيمُ
(Do not forbid a trait while doing the like of it; it is a great disgrace on you when you do.)
The second is that it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the first. This second view is preferable, because it contains a prohibition of each one separately, unlike the first, which is a prohibition of combining the two; and a prohibition of combining two things does not necessarily entail a prohibition of each one separately. The treatment of this has already been given at {وَتَكْتُمُواْ الحق} [al-Baqara: 42], at the beginning of al-Baqara.
«أماناتِكم» is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "those entrusted with your trusts" (aṣḥāba amānātikum). It is also possible that they were forbidden to betray the trusts themselves, by way of exaggeration, as though the trusts had been made things that are betrayed. Mujāhid read «أمانتكم» in the singular, and it was also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, the plural being meant.
«وأنتم تعلمون» is a ḥāl clause. The object of the knowing may be intended, that is: "you know the ugliness of that," or "that you will be held to account for it." It is also possible not to supply one, that is: "you are among those possessed of knowledge." The knowing may be taken in its ordinary sense, or in the sense of recognition (ʿirfān).

semin-durr:29-29.t:
The discussion of «الفرقان» has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara. What is meant by it here is that which brings one out of error, or the thing that separates truth from falsehood. Mazrad ibn Ḍirār said:
2405 - بادَرَ الأفقَ أن يغيبَ فلمَّا ... أظلم الليلُ لم يَجِدْ فُرْقانا
(He hastened to the horizon before it should vanish; but when the night grew dark he found no deliverance [furqān].)
Another said:
2406 - ما لك مِنْ طولِ الأَسى فُرْقانُ ... بعد قَطينٍ رحلوا وبانُوا
(You have no relief [furqān] from long grief after the household that departed and went away.)
Another said:
2407 - وكيف أُرَجِّي الخلدَ والموتُ طالبي ... وما ليَ من كأسِ المنية فرقانُ
(How can I hope for immortality while death is seeking me, and I have no escape [furqān] from the cup of death?)

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ}: This adverbial is conjoined to the adverbial before it, and «ليُثْبتوك» is attached to «يَمْكُرُ». "Fixing" (tathbīt) here means striking until the one struck has no movement left. He said:
2408 - فقلت وَيْحَكَ ماذا في صحيفتكمْ ... قالوا الخليفةُ أمسى مُثْبَتاً وجِعا
(I said, "Woe to you, what is in your letter?" They said, "The caliph has become laid low, in pain.")
Ibn Wathāb read «لِيُثَبِّتوك», making the verb transitive by doubling the middle radical. Al-Nakhaʿī read «ليُبَيِّتُوك», from bayāt (night attack).

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هُوَ الحق}: The majority read «الحق» in the accusative; it is the khabar of "to be" (kawn) and «هو» is a separator pronoun (faṣl), which has already been treated at length. Al-Akhfash said «هو» is redundant (zāʾid), meaning what was said before, that it is a faṣl. Al-Aʿmash and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «الحق» in the nominative; the explanation is clear: «هو» is nominative as mubtadaʾ and «الحق» is its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of "to be," as in his saying:
2409 - ... تَحِنُّ إلى ليلى وأنت تركتَها
وكنتَ عليها بالمَلا أنت أقدرُ
(... You long for Laylā though you left her, and you were more able [to keep] her in the open country.)
This is the dialect of Tamīm. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In Arabic it is permissible to put «الحق» in the nominative as the khabar of «هو», the sentence being the khabar of «كان»." Al-Zajjāj said: "I do not know anyone who read with this permissible form." I say: it has become clear who read it so, and they are two eminent men.
His saying: {مِنْ عِندِكَ} is a ḥāl from the meaning of «الحق», that is: "the established, in the state of its being from You." His saying {مِّنَ السمآء} has two views. One is that it is attached to the verb before it. The second is that it is an adjective of «حجارة», so it is attached to an omitted word. As for their saying «من السماء» although rain comes only from it, al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as if he wanted it to be said, 'then rain down upon us sijjīl,' and he put «حجارة من السماء» in its place, as one says 'he poured over him a masrūda of iron,' meaning 'a coat of mail.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "He means by that emphasis," and said: "just as the meaning of «من حديد» is emphasis, because a masrūd (riveted) thing is only of iron, as rain is only from the sky." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Their saying «من السماء» is exaggeration and hyperbole." The Shaykh said: "What appears is that the wisdom in their saying «من السماء» is that they were matching the coming of the rain from the direction from which he, peace be upon him, had said revelation comes to him; that is: 'You claim that revelation comes to you from the sky, so bring us punishment from the direction from which revelation comes to you.' They said it in order to deem it far-fetched."

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ}: The discussion of this lām, called lām al-juḥūd (the lām of denial), has already been given. The majority read it with kasra. Abū l-Sammāl read it with fatḥa. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from Abū Zayd: "I heard some of the Arabs say «لَيعذبهم» with fatḥa on the lām; it is an unfamiliar dialect, not used in the Qur'an." I say: he means in the well-known reading, and he did not count the reading of Abū l-Sammāl. Ibn Mujāhid reported from Abū Zayd the fatḥa of every lām from some Arabs, except in «الحمد لله». ʿAbd al-Wārith reported from Abū ʿAmr the fatḥa of the lām of command in {فَلْيَنظُرِ الإنسان إلى طَعَامِهِ} [ʿAbasa: 24].
He brought the khabar of the first «كان» differently from how he brought it in the second. It is either omitted, namely "intending" (irāda), as the Basrans supply it, that is: "Allah was not intending to punish them" — and the negation of the intention of punishment is more emphatic than the negation of punishment — or else he emphasised it with the lām, in the view of the Kufans, because his being among them is a stronger reason than their seeking forgiveness; for the difference is great between his, peace be upon him, presence among them and their seeking forgiveness.
His saying: {وَأَنتَ فِيهِمْ} is a ḥāl, and likewise {وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ}. The apparent view is that all the pronouns refer to the disbelievers. It was also said that the pronoun in «يُعَذِّبهم» and «مُعَذِّبهم» refers to the disbelievers, while the pronoun in «وهم» refers to the believers. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وهم يستغفرون» is in the position of ḥāl, and its meaning is the negation of seeking forgiveness from them; that is: if they were of those who believe and seek forgiveness for disbelief, He would not have punished them, as in the saying of the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ القرى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ} [Hūd: 114]; but they do not seek forgiveness and do not believe, and that is not expected of them." This meaning that he mentioned is transmitted from Qatāda and Abū Zayd, and Ibn Jarīr preferred it.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أن لا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ}: There are two views on «أن». The first, which is the apparent one, is that it is a maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya), and its position is either accusative or genitive, because it is on the omission of the preposition; the implied form is: "in that He not punish them." This preposition and its genitive noun are attached to what «لهم» is attached to, namely being established; the implied meaning is: "what has been established for them concerning Allah's not punishing them," meaning that they have no share in the absence of punishment. The second is that it is redundant (zāʾida), which is the view of al-Akhfash. Al-Naḥḥās said: "If it were as he said, it would have made «يُعَذِّبهم» nominative." That is, the verb should have been nominative as standing in the position of ḥāl, as in {وَمَا لَنَا لاَ نُؤْمِنُ بالله} [al-Māʾida: 84]. But redundancy does not entail absence of effect; do you not see that «مِنْ» and the bāʾ operate although they are added? Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said that it is a ḥāl, but that is remote, because «أَنْ» makes the verb exclusively future." The apparent view is that «ما» in «وما لهم» is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) and is an interrogative with the meaning of affirmation, that is: "How should they not be punished while they are characterised by this state?" It was also said that «ما» is negative, so it is a statement of that, that is: it is not the case that there is no punishment, i.e. punishment is not removed from them while they are engaged in this state.
His saying: {وَمَا كانوا أَوْلِيَآءَهُ}: There are two views on this sentence. One is that it is resumptive, and the hāʾ refers to the mosque, that is: "they were not the guardians of the mosque." The second is that it is conjoined to the preceding ḥāl clause, which is «وهم يَصُدُّون», and the meaning is: how should Allah not punish them while they are characterised by these two attributes: their barring from the Sacred Mosque and their not being its guardians? It is also possible that the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted, that is: "they were not Allah's guardians."
[Translator's note: the source text has «هذبن» in «هذبن الوَصْفَيْن», evidently a misprint for «هذين»; translated as "these two".]

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مُكَآءً وَتَصْدِيَةً}: That is: nothing of what they count as prayer and worship was anything but these two acts, namely mukāʾ and taṣdiya; that is, if they had a prayer, it was nothing but these two, as in the poet's saying:
2410 - وما كنت أخشى أن يكونَ عطاؤُه ... أداهِمَ سُوداً أو مُحَدْرَجَةً سُمْرا
(I never feared that his gift would be black fetters or tightly twisted brown whips.)
He put the fetters and the whips in the place of the gift.
Al-mukāʾ is the maṣdar of makā yamkū, that is: he whistled between his fingers or between his palms. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "I said to Musajjiʿ ibn Nabhān: 'What is meant by "his farīṣa makes a mukāʾ sound"?' So he interlaced his fingers, put them to his mouth and blew into them." I say: he means the saying of ʿAntara:
2411 - وحَليلِ غانيةٍ تركتُ مُجَدَّلاً ... تَمْكُو فريصتُه كشِدْق الأَعْلَمِ
(Many a husband of a fair woman I left sprawled, his farīṣa whistling like the split lip of a hare-lipped man.)
It is said: makat al-farīṣa, that is: it made a sound with the blood. And makat ist al-dābba, that is: it blew out wind. Mujāhid said: al-mukkāʾ is a whistling in the tune of a white bird found in the Hijaz. The poet said:
2412 - إذا غرَّد المُكَّاء في غير روضةٍ ... فويلٌ لأهل الشَّاءِ والحُمُرات
(When the mukkāʾ warbles in a place that is not a meadow, then woe to the owners of sheep and donkeys.)
Al-mukkāʾ is of the form fuʿʿāl, a pattern of intensity. Abū ʿUbayda said: "One says makā yamkū mukūwan and mukāʾan: he whistled. Al-mukāʾ with ḍamma is like al-bukāʾ and al-ṣurākh." It was said that of the names of sounds only al-ghināʾ and al-nidāʾ depart from this by taking kasra.
As for al-taṣdiya, there are two views on it. The first is that it is from al-ṣadā, which is the echo of a voice heard in empty hard places. From it one says ṣadiya yaṣdā taṣdiya, and what is meant by it here is the sound of clapping, of one hand against the other. In the exegesis: when the polytheists heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying and reciting the Qur'an, they clapped their hands and whistled with their mouths, to distract those who were listening to him and to confuse his recitation. This fits his saying: {لاَ تَسْمَعُواْ لهذا القرآن والغوا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ} [Fuṣṣilat: 26]. It was also said that it is derived from taṣdida, which is uproar, shouting and clapping, and that one of the two dāls was replaced by yāʾ for lightness. What indicates this is his saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ} [al-Zukhruf: 57] in the reading of those who read the ṣād with kasra, that is: they raise an uproar and clamour. This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda. Abū Jaʿfar al-Rustumī rejected it and said: "It is only from al-ṣadā, so how can it be made from a geminated root?" Abū ʿAlī rejected Abū Jaʿfar's rejection and said: "It is established that yaṣuddūn is of the kind of sound, so its derivation is from that, and taṣdiya is of the form tafʿila," and then he said much more. The second view is that it is from al-ṣadd, which is prevention, the original being taṣdida with two dāls too, the second of which was replaced by yāʾ. What supports this is the reading of those who read «يَصُدُّون» with ḍamma, that is: they prevent.
The majority read «صلاتُهم» in the nominative and «مُكاءً» in the accusative. Abān ibn Taghlib, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim, with a difference reported from them, read «وما كان صلاتَهم» with «صلاتَهم» accusative and «مكاءٌ» nominative. Al-Fārisī judged this reading wrong and said: "It is not permissible to predicate a definite noun of an indefinite one except out of necessity, as in the saying of Ḥassān:
2413 - كأنَّ سَبيئةً مِنْ بيت رَأْسٍ ... يكونُ مزاجَها عَسَلٌ وماءُ
(As if wine from Bayt Raʾs, its mixture being honey and water.)"
Abū l-Fatḥ explained it on the basis that al-mukāʾ and al-taṣdiya are generic nouns (ism jins), meaning that they are two maṣdars. He said: "In a generic noun the definite and the indefinite are close to each other, so why should it be said that one of the two is made the subject and the other the predicate?" This is close to the noun defined by generic «أل» when it is described by a sentence, as an indefinite is described by it, as in his saying, the Exalted: {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الليل نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النهار} [Yā Sīn: 37], and the saying of the other:
2414 - ولقد مَرَرْتُ على اللئيم يَسُبُّني ... فَمَضَيْتُ ثُمَّتَ قلتُ لا يَعْنيني
(I passed by the base man as he was abusing me; I went on, then said, "He does not mean me.")
Some of them said: "Abū ʿAmr read «إلا مُكاً» with the short form and tanwīn; this is as they said bukāʾ and bukā, with long and short vowel." The poet combined the two forms:
2415 - بَكَتْ عيني وحُقَّ لها بُكاها ... وما يُغْني البكاءُ ولا العويلُ
(My eye wept, and it has the right to its weeping; but neither weeping nor wailing avails.)
[Translator's note: in the source the quotation of "some of them said" is opened but never closed, and this entry ends there.]

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَمِيزَ الله الخبيث}: The disagreement about it has already been given in Āl ʿImrān. His saying «ويَجْعل»: it may be taken as meaning "to make into" (taṣyīr), governing two objects, or as meaning "to cast," governing one. On either reading «بعضه» is a badal baʿḍ min kull (partial substitute), and on the first view «على بعض» is in the position of the second object, while on the second it is attached to the act of placing itself, as in your saying "you placed your goods, some of them upon others." Abū l-Baqāʾ, after ruling that it takes one object, said: "It was also said that the preposition and its genitive noun is a ḥāl, the implied form being: 'and He places the vile one, some of it high above some.'"
The lām in «ليميز» is attached to «يُحشرون». One says mayyaztuhu fa-tamayyaza and miztuhu fa-immāza. It was also read anomalously {وانمازوا اليوم} [Yā Sīn: 59]. Abū Zayd recited:
2416 - لمَّا نبا اللهُ عني شرَّ غَدْرتِه ... وانْمِزْتُ لا مُنْسِئاً غَدْراً ولا وَجِلا
(When Allah turned away from me the evil of his treachery, and I separated myself, neither postponing treachery nor fearful.)
The difference between these words has already been given in Āl ʿImrān.
His saying: {فَيَرْكُمَهُ} is conjoined to the accusative before it. Al-rakm is your gathering one thing upon another until it becomes a heap (rukām) and heaped up (markūm), as sand and cloud are heaped; from it {يَقُولُواْ سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ} [al-Ṭūr: 44]. Al-murtakam is the main road, because of the heaping (rakm) in it, that is: the crowding of the passers-by and their tracks. «جميعاً» is a ḥāl. According to some it may be tawkīd (emphasis).

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِلَّذِينَ كفروا}: There are the two well-known views on this lām. The first is that it is for conveying (tablīgh): he was commanded to convey to them the meaning of this sentence quoted after "say," whether he gave it in this wording or in another wording conveying its meaning. The second is that it is causal (taʿlīl), which is what al-Zamakhsharī said, and he denied that it is for conveying, saying: "That is: say this saying on their account: if they desist. Had it meant that he should address them with it, it would have been said: 'If you desist, He will forgive you,' which is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd. Similar to it is {وَقَالَ الذين كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لَوْ كَانَ خَيْراً مَّا سَبَقُونَآ} [al-Aḥqāf: 11]: they addressed it to others, [on their account,] so that they might hear it."
«يَغْفر» was also read in the active voice, the subject being a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying, the Exalted: «{وَيَكُونَ}: The majority read it in the accusative, conjoined to the accusative before it. Al-Aʿmash read it in the nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf). Al-Ḥasan, Yaʿqūb and Sulaymān ibn Salām read «بما تَعْملون» with the tāʾ of address, while the rest read it with the yāʾ of the third person.
[Translator's note: the source text opens with a stray slash and an opening quotation mark, «/ «», before {وَيَكُونَ}; they are reproduced as a mark only.]

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَنَّ الله مَوْلاَكُمْ نِعْمَ المولى}: Two views are possible for «مولاكم». The more apparent is that «مولاكم» is the khabar and «نِعْم المولى» is an independent sentence brought for praise. The second is that it is a badal from «الله», and the sentence of praise is the khabar of «أن», the one praised (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) being omitted, that is: "excellent is the Patron: Allah," or "your Lord."

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {واعلموا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُم}: The apparent view is that this «ما» is a relative (mawṣūla) meaning "that which" (alladhī). It should properly have been written separated from «أنَّ», as {إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ لآتٍ} [al-Anʿām: 134] is written separately, but it was written thus in the Uthmanic orthography. «غَنِمْتم» is its ṣila, and its returning pronoun is omitted since the conditions for omission are fulfilled, that is: "ghanimtumūhu." His saying {فأنَّ الله}: the fāʾ is redundant in the khabar, because the mubtadaʾ is made to contain the meaning of a condition, and it does no harm that an operator (nāsikh) has entered upon it, because it did not change its meaning; this is like his saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين فَتَنُواْ} [al-Burūj: 10], and then He said: «فلهم». Al-Akhfash, although he allows the redundant fāʾ in the khabar of a mubtadaʾ without restriction, forbids it with a relative noun resembling a condition when the kasra-form «إنَّ» enters upon it; the verse of al-Burūj is evidence against him. Once this is established, «أنَّ» and what it governs is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "then it is obligatory that to Allah belongs a fifth of it," and the sentence made of this mubtadaʾ and khabar is the khabar of «أنَّ». The apparent sense of the Shaykh's words is that he made the fāʾ enter upon «أن لله خُمُسَه» without supposing that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, but made it a khabar in itself; that is not what he intends, since this fāʾ does not enter upon a single word but upon a sentence. What supports that this is his intention is what I mentioned, that he reported al-Zamakhsharī's view, namely that he supposed that «أنَّ» and what is within its scope is a mubtadaʾ with omitted khabar, and he made this a view additional to what he had put forward earlier.
It is also possible that «ما» is conditional (sharṭiyya), its governing word being «غَنِمْتُم» after it; the ism of «أنَّ» is then the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), which is the school of al-Farrāʾ. But this is not allowed by the Basrans except out of necessity, on condition that it is not followed by a verb, as in his saying:
2417 - إنَّ مَن يدخلِ الكنيسةِ يوماً ... يَلْقَ فيها جآذِراً وظِباءَ
(Whoever enters the church one day will meet in it fawns and gazelles.)
and the saying of the other:
2418 - إنَّ مَنْ لام في بني بنتِ حَسَّا ... نَ أَلُمْهُ وأَعْصِهِ في الخُطوبِ
(Whoever blames the sons of the daughter of Ḥassān, I shall blame him and disobey him in times of calamity.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is garbled in the source as «241 - 8-»; it is evidently 2418.]
It was also said that the fāʾ is redundant and that the second «أن» is a badal from the first. Makkī said: "It was said that the second is an emphasis for the first, but that is not permissible, because the first «أنَّ» would remain without a khabar, and because the fāʾ comes between the emphasised and the emphasiser, and its redundancy is not good in such a place." It was also said that «ما» is a maṣdar particle and the maṣdar has the meaning of a passive participle, that is: "that what you have taken as spoil [is] the direct object," that is: "and know that your ghunm, i.e. your maghnūm (what is taken as spoil)."
His saying: {مِّن شَيْءٍ} is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the returning pronoun of the relative, which is implied; the meaning is: "what you have taken as spoil, being of anything," that is: little or much. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from al-Juʿfī from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and another reported from al-Juʿfī from Hārūn from Abū ʿAmr: «فإن لله» with kasra on the hamza. What supports this reading is the reading of al-Nakhaʿī «فللَّه خمسُه», which is a resumption. Abū l-Baqāʾ explained it as meaning that it and what is within its scope is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the first «أنَّ».
Al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd al-Wārith from Abū ʿAmr read «خُمْسَه» (with sukūn), which is a good lightening. Al-Juʿfī read «خِمْسَه». They said: its explanation is that he made the khāʾ follow the vowel of what precedes it, which is the hāʾ of the divine Name, from another independent word. They said: it is like the reading of those who read {والسمآء ذَاتِ الحبك} [al-Dhāriyāt: 7] with kasra on the ḥāʾ, following the kasra of the tāʾ of «ذات», and they did not count the sākin, which is the lām of definiteness, because it is a weak barrier. I wish I knew how al-Juʿfī reads, given this: if he reads thus with ḍamma on the mīm, it is extremely heavy because it moves from kasra to ḍamma; and if he reads it with sukūn, which is the apparent case, then he transmitted it as a reading from Abū ʿAmr or from ʿĀṣim; but the one who read «ذاتِ الحِبك» keeps the ḍamma of the bāʾ, which leads to the pattern fiʿul, with kasra on the first radical and ḍamma on the second, a rejected pattern. I said he reads it that way only because, had he read with kasra on the bāʾ, they would have had no need to interpret his reading as following, since «الحبك» has two forms: ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the bāʾ, or kasra on both; so much so that some claimed that the reading of "moving out of a kasra to a ḍamma" is from tadākhul (the overlapping of the two forms). [Translator's note: the Arabic wording here is terse and possibly corrupt.]
Al-ghanīma originally comes from al-ghunm, which is success, and that originally comes from al-ghanam, the well-known animal (sheep), for gaining it is called ghunm; then the usage was extended and everything gained was called ghunm, maghnam and ghanīma. ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada said:
2419 - ومُطْعَمُ الغُنْم يومَ الغُنْمِ مَطْعَمُه ... أنَّى توجَّه والمحرومُ محرومُ
(He is one who feeds on spoil on the day of spoil, wherever he turns, while the deprived remains deprived.)
Another said:
2420 - لقد طَوَّفْتُ في الآفاق حتى ... رَضِيتُ من الغنيمة بالإِياب
(I have roamed the horizons until I was content, in place of booty, with returning.)
His saying: {إِن كُنتُمْ} is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb) is implied, according to the majority, not preceding; that is: "if you have believed, then know that the ruling on the fifth is as stated before," or "then accept what you have been commanded."
His saying: {وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا}: «ما» is conjoined to the divine Name, so it is genitive in position, and its returning pronoun is omitted. Some claimed that the apodosis of the condition precedes it, namely his saying «فنِعْم المَولى»; this is not permissible by the principles of the Basrans.
His saying {يَوْمَ الفرقان}: Three views are possible. The first is that it is accusative by «أَنْزلنا», that is: "We sent it down on the day of Badr, on which truth and falsehood were separated." The second is that it is accusative by his saying «آمنتم», that is: "if you believed on the Day of al-Furqān." Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The third is that it may be accusative by «غَنِمْتُمْ». Al-Zajjāj said: "That is: what you took as spoil on the Day of al-Furqān, its ruling is thus and thus." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is a good interpretation in meaning, but it is objected to by the fact that it separates the adverbial from what governs it by this sentence of many words." I say: it is also barred from another angle, more specific than this: «ما» is either conditional, as is the view of al-Farrāʾ, or relative. On the first, it leads to separation between the verb of the condition and its object by the apodosis sentence and its attachments; on the second, it leads to separation between the verb of the ṣila and its object by the khabar of «أنَّ».
His saying: {يَوْمَ التقى الجمعان} has two views. One is that it is a badal from the adverbial before it. The second is that it is accusative by «الفرقان», since it is a maṣdar, as if it were said: "the day on which the separation was made, on the day the two armies met," that is: the separation on the day of the meeting of the two armies. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «عُبُدنا» with two ḍammas, which is the plural of ʿabd, just as {وَعُبُدَ الطاغوت} [al-Māʾida: 60] was read. What is meant by al-ʿubud in this reading here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those of the believers who followed him.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ أَنتُمْ}: There are four views on this adverbial. The first is that it is accusative by an implied «اذكروا»; this is the view of al-Zajjāj. The second is that it is also a badal from «يوم الفرقان». The third is that it is accusative by «قدير», which is not clear, since His being described as able is not restricted to any particular adverbial. The fourth is that it is accusative by «الفرقان», that is: "He separated truth from falsehood when you were on the near bank."
His saying: {بالعدوة} is attached to an omitted word because it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the bāʾ has the meaning of «في», as in your saying "Zayd is in Mecca" (Zayd bi-Makka). Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «بالعِدوة» with kasra on the ʿayn in both places; the rest read with ḍamma in both. They are two dialectal forms meaning the bank of the valley, its edge and its side; it was so called because it restrains (ʿadat) what is in the valley, of water and the like, from passing beyond it, that is, it prevents it. The poet said:
2421 - عَدَتْني عن زيارتها العَوادي ... وحالَتْ دونَها حربٌ زَبُونُ
(Obstacles kept me from visiting her, and a fierce, grinding war came between us.)
Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Qatāda and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read it with fatḥa; all are dialectal forms of one meaning. This is the view of the majority of the lexicographers. However, Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ denied the ḍamma and al-Akhfash agreed with him, saying: "Only the kasra was heard from the Arabs." Abū ʿUbayd reported both forms but said: "The ḍamma is the more frequent of the two." Al-Yazīdī said: "The kasra is the dialect of the Hijaz," and recited the saying of Aws ibn Ḥajar:
2422 - وفارسٍ لم يَحُلَّ القوم عِدْوَتَه ... وَلَّوا سِراعاً وما هَمُّوا بإقبال
(Many a horseman whose position the people could not shift; they turned back quickly and did not think of advancing.)
with kasra and ḍamma. This is what should be said: there is no ground for denying the ḍamma or the kasra, because each is mutawātir (widely transmitted). Abū ʿAmr's statement is taken to mean that it had not reached him. It is also possible to say, of the reading of those who read with fatḥa on the ʿayn, that it is a maṣdar by which the place was named.
It was also read anomalously «بالعِدْية», turning the wāw into yāʾ because of the kasra before it; the intervening letter is not counted because it is sākin, hence a weak barrier. This is as they said "he is my cousin dinyā" (ibn ʿammī dinyā) with kasra on the dāl, from dunuww (nearness); likewise qinya and ṣibya, whose origin is safe (from change), like dhirwa, ṣifwa and ribwa. As for his saying «الدنيا», the discussion of this word has already been given.
His saying: {القصوى} is the feminine of al-aqṣā. Al-aqṣā means the farthest. Al-qaṣw means distance. The morphologists have two formulations, the more frequent of which is that fuʿlā from roots with wāw: if it is a noun, its lām is replaced by yāʾ; then they give examples such as al-dunyā, al-ʿulyā and al-quṣyā — and these are adjectives, because they are of the pattern of the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl); the excuse for them seems to be that although these are originally adjectives, they have been treated as inert nouns. They said: if fuʿlā is an adjective, its lām is left as it is, like al-ḥulwā, the feminine of al-aḥlā; and they stated explicitly that al-quṣwā is irregular (shādhdha) although it is the dialect of the Hijaz, and that al-quṣyā is regular, being the dialect of Tamīm. Among those who stated that al-quṣwā is irregular is Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sikkīt. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for al-quṣwā, it is like al-qawad in coming on the original form. Al-quṣyā has also occurred, but the use of al-quṣwā is more frequent, as the use of istaṣwaba became frequent although istaṣāba has occurred, and aghīlat although aghālat." End of quotation.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «بالعُدْوَة والقُصْيا», bringing it in the dialect of Tamīm, which is the regular form according to these scholars.
The second formulation, which is the less common, the converse, is: if it is an adjective it is changed, such as al-ʿulyā, al-dunyā and al-quṣyā; if it is a noun it is left, such as Ḥuzwā, as in his saying:
2423 - أداراً بحُزْوَى هِجْتِ للعين عَبْرةً ... فماءُ الهوى يَرْفَضُّ أو يَتَرَقْرَقُ
(Did an abode at Ḥuzwā stir tears in your eye, so that the water of longing now streams or trickles?)
On this basis al-ḥulwā is irregular, since its lām is left though it is an adjective, and so is al-quṣwā according to these scholars, because it is an adjective.
It follows from these two formulations that «قُصْوى» is contrary to the rule in both, and that «قُصْيا» is the rule, because according to the first group it belongs to the nouns, and they change it to yāʾ, and according to the second group it belongs to the adjectives, and they also change it to yāʾ. The difference shows only in al-ḥulwā and Ḥuzwā: al-ḥulwā, according to the first group, is regular in keeping the wāw, because it is an adjective, and irregular according to the second group, because for them an adjective has its wāw turned into yāʾ; Ḥuzwā is the opposite: the first group apply the change to nouns and not to adjectives, and the second group the reverse. This is a good point on which many people become confused, so I have refined it. By "irregularity" we mean irregularity against the rule, not irregularity of usage; do you not see the mutawātir usage of al-quṣwā?
His saying: {والركب أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ}: The best view of this wāw, and the wāw before it that enters upon «هم», is that what follows is conjoined to «أنتم», because it is the beginning of a classification of their circumstances and the circumstances of their enemy. It is also possible that both are wāws of ḥāl. «أسفل» is accusative as an adverbial standing in place of the khabar, and it is in reality an adjective of an omitted adverb of place, that is: "and the caravan was in a place lower than your place." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أسفلُ» in the nominative, by way of latitude (ittisāʿ), making the adverbial itself the caravan, for exaggeration and latitude. Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ, al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī allowed «أسفلُ» in the nominative on the supposition of an omitted word, that is: 'the place of the caravan is lower.'" The first explanation is more emphatic in meaning.
Al-rakb is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for rākib (rider), not a broken plural of it, contrary to al-Akhfash, because of the saying:
2424 - بَنَيْتُه مِنْ عُصْبَةٍ مِنْ مالِيا ... أخشى رُكَيْباً أو رُجَيْلاً غاديا
(I built it with a band out of my own wealth; I fear a small party of riders or a small party on foot coming at dawn.)
For he formed the diminutive on its own form, and had it been a plural it would not have been diminutivised on its own form.
His saying: {ولكن لِّيَقْضِيَ}: «ليَقْضي» is attached to an omitted word, that is: "but you met in order that He might decree." Al-Zamakhsharī supplied the omitted word, saying: "That is: that Allah might decree a matter which had to be carried out, namely the victory of His friends and the subjugation of His enemies; He planned that."
«كان» may be in its ordinary sense of indicating that the content of the sentence is joined to past time, or it may mean «صار» (became), indicating transformation, that is: it became done after it had not been so.
His saying: {لِّيَهْلِكَ}: There are several views. The first is that it is a badal from His saying «ليقضيَ», with repetition of the governing particle, so it is attached to what the first is attached to.
The second is that it is attached to His saying «مفعولاً», that is: He did this matter for such-and-such reasons. The third is that it is attached to what «ليقضيَ» is attached to, by conjunction to it with an omitted conjunction, its implied form being «وليهلك»; the conjunction is omitted, which is very rare. I have drawn attention to this earlier. The fourth is that it is attached to «يَقْضي»; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. Al-Aʿmash and ʿIṣma, from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, read «ليهلَكَ» with fatḥa on the lām (of the verb); the analogical past of this would be halika with kasra, but the well-known form is the fatḥa: He said, the Exalted: {إِن امرؤ هَلَكَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 176] and {حتى إِذَا هَلَكَ} [Ghāfir: 34].
His saying: {مَنْ حَيَّ}: Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr read it with the unassimilated (iẓhār) form; the rest read it assimilated (idghām). Iẓhār and idghām in this kind are two well-known dialectal forms: it is every past verb ending in two yāʾs, the first of which has kasra, such as ḥayiya and ʿayiya. From the idghām is the saying of al-Mutalammis:
2425 - فهذا أَوانُ العِرْضِ حَيَّ ذُبابُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(This is the season of the valley-land, its flies alive ...)
and the other said:
2426 - عَيُّوا بأمرِهِمُ كما ... عَيَّتْ ببيضَتِها الحمامَهْ
(They were at a loss over their affair as the dove is at a loss over her egg.)
So he assimilated «عيُّوا», and it is also recited ʿayyat and ʿayiyat, assimilated and unassimilated. Whoever uses iẓhār does so because it is the original, and because idghām leads to doubling the weak letter, which is heavy in itself; and because the first yāʾ must be pronounced separately in some forms, namely the imperfect of this verb, due to the second turning into alif in yaḥyā and yaʿyā, so the past is carried over to it to keep the chapter consistent; and because the vowel on the second is accidental, being lost in ḥayītu and its like; and because the two vowels differ, and difference of the two vowels is like difference of the two letters. They said: for that reason they said laḥiḥat ʿaynuhu, ḍabiba l-makān, alila l-siqāʾ and mashishat al-dābba. Sībawayh said: "Yūnus informed us of this dialect," meaning the dialect of iẓhār. He said: "I heard some of the Arabs say aḥyiyāʾ and aḥyiya, pronouncing them separately." If it is not assimilated when the vowel is permanent, then with its being accidental it is all the more so. As for the one who assimilates, it is because of the heaviness of a kasra appearing on a letter of the same kind, and because the vowel of the second is permanent, being a vowel of construction (binā), and its loss in ḥayītu does no harm, as it does no harm in sound verbs where idghām is obligatory, such as ḥalaltu and ẓalaltu. All this applies where the vowel is a vowel of construction, and for that reason it was restricted to the past; but when it is a vowel of declension (iʿrāb), only iẓhār is allowed, as in yuḥyiya and lan yuʿyiya.
His saying: {عَن بَيِّنَةٍ} is attached to «يَهْلِكَ» and «يَحْيَا». Destruction and life are expressions for faith and disbelief. The meaning is: that the disbelief of the one who disbelieves may issue from clarity and evidence, not from the entanglement of doubt, and that the Islam of the one who submits may issue from clarity, not from the entanglement of doubt.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ الله}: The governing word of «إذ» may be implied, that is: "remember"; or it may be «عليم», though this is remote since this attribute would be restricted to this time. It is also possible that this «إذ» is a badal from the «إذ» before it.
The showing (irāʾa) here is dream-vision (ḥulmiyya), and the grammarians differed over it: does it originally take one object, like the sight-verb (baṣariyya), or two, like the verbs of opinion (ẓanniyya)? The majority hold the first. When the transitivising hamza enters, it gives it a second or a third object, according to the two views. On the first, the kāf is the first object and «هم» the second, and «قليلاً» is a ḥāl; on the second, «قليلاً» is accusative as the third object. The latter is invalidated by the fact that the third may be omitted in this chapter for mere abbreviation (iqtiṣāran), that is, without any indication; you say "Allah showed me Zayd in my sleep" and "I saw him in sleep"; had it taken three objects, it would not be omitted for abbreviation, because it is originally a khabar.

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ}: The showing here is by sight (baṣariyya). Supplying the ṣila of the plural mīm (the wāw) is obligatory here because of its attachment to a pronoun. Neither sukūn nor ḍamma without wāw is allowed. Yūnus allowed that, saying "antum ḍarabtumuh" for «ضربتموه», with sukūn on the mīm or with ḍamma. He may be strengthened by what was reported from ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him: «أراهُمُني الباطل شيطاناً» ("falsehood showed them me as a devil"). There is an irregularity in this statement from another angle: the precedence of the less specific pronoun over the more specific while attached.

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying, the Exalted: {فَتَفْشَلُواْ}: Two views are possible. The first is accusative as the answer to a prohibition. The second is jussive, conjoined to the verb of prohibition before it. Both have already been treated in «وتَخُونوا» earlier. What indicates the second is the reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar «ويَذْهَبُ» with the yāʾ of the third person and the jussive. Abū l-Baqāʾ reported the jussive reading without specifying the yāʾ of the third person. Abū Ḥaywa, Abān and ʿIṣma read «ويَذْهَبَ» with the yāʾ of the third person and the accusative. Al-Ḥasan read «فَتَفْشِلوا» with kasra on the shīn. Abū Ḥātim said: "This is not known," while others said it is a second dialectal form.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بَطَراً وَرِئَآءَ}: Both are accusative as mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). It is also possible that they are two maṣdars in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the subject of «خرجوا», that is: "they went out exultantly and showing off." «رئاء» is a maṣdar annexed to its object.
His saying: {وَيَصُدُّونَ} may be resumptive, or it may be conjoined to «بطراً» and «رئاء», because it is interpreted as a ḥāl, that is: "exultant, showing off and barring people"; the object is omitted because it is indicated, or he disregarded it.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ}: That is: remember the time of the adorning. «قال» may be conjoined to «زَيَّن», or the wāw may be a wāw of ḥāl, with «قد» implied after the wāw according to those who require that.
His saying: {لاَ غَالِبَ لَكُمُ}: «لكم» is the khabar of «لا», so it is attached to an omitted word, and «اليوم» is accusative by what the khabar is attached to. It is not allowed that «لكم» or the adverbial be attached to «غالب», because it would then be "extended" (muṭawwal), and whenever it is extended it is put in the accusative.
His saying: {مِنَ الناس} is an explanation (bayān) of the kind of the victor. It was also said that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم», since it contains the meaning of being established. Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade «من الناس» to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «غالب», saying: "because the ism of «لا», when it governs what follows it, is put in the accusative." And the matter is so.
His saying: {وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ}: This sentence may be conjoined to His saying «لا غالبَ لكم», so that a negated sentence is conjoined to another negated sentence. The wāw may also be for ḥāl. The alif of «جار» comes from a wāw, from their saying «تجاوروا», and the treatment of this has already been given. «لكم» is attached to an omitted word, since it is an adjective of «جار»; it may also be attached to «جار» because of the meaning of the verb in it.
Al-rīḥ (wind) in {ريحكم} is a metonym for power (dawla) and victory. He said:
2427 - إذا هَبَّتْ رياحُكَ فاغتنِمْها ... فإنَّ لكلِّ عاصفةٍ سكونا
(When your winds blow, seize them, for every gale has its lull.)
Abū ʿUbayd transmitted it as «ركوداً». Another said:
2428 - أتَنْظُران قليلاً رَيْثَ غَفْلَتِهِمْ ... أم تَعْدُوانِ فإن الريح للعادي
(Will you two wait a little for the moment of their inattention, or will you run, for the wind is for the one who runs?)
And he said:
2429 - قد عَوَّدَتْهمْ ظُباهمْ أن يكونَ لهم ... ريحُ القتالِ وأسلابُ الذين لَقُوا
(Their blades have accustomed them that theirs be the wind of battle and the spoils of those they met.)
It was also said that al-rīḥ means awe, which is close to the first, as in his saying:
2430 - كما حَمَيْناك يوم النَّعْفِ مِنْ شَطَطٍ ... والفضلُ للقوم مِنْ ريحٍ ومن عَدَدِ
(As we protected you on the day of al-Naʿf from injustice, while the advantage went to the people in power and numbers.)
His saying: «نَكَص» is the answer to «لمَّا». Al-nukūṣ: al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "Going back backwards, fleeing." Some said: this is its origin, but it was extended until it was used for any retreat, even if not backwards. The poet said:
2431 - هم يضربون حَبِيْكَ البَيْضِ إذ لَحِقُوا ... لا يَنْكُصُون إذا ما استُلْحِموا لَحِموا
(They strike the plaited chain of the helmets when they catch up; they do not retreat when they are overwhelmed, but are slain.)
Al-Muʾarrij said: "Al-nukūṣ is returning, in the dialect of Sulaym." The poet said:
2432 - ليس النكوصُ على الأَعْقابِ مَكْرُمَةً ... إن المكارمَ إقدامٌ على الأَسَلِ
(Turning back on one's heels is no noble act; noble deeds are charging upon the spear-points.)
By this he means only absolute returning, because it is a metonym for flight, and there is room for objection in it, because in most flight in battle it is, as mentioned, a backward retreat. «على عَقِبيْه» is a ḥāl: either corroborative (muʾakkida) according to those who restrict it to going backwards, or foundational (muʾassisa) according to those who use it for absolute returning.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إذ يقولُ}: The governing word of «إذ» is either «زَيَّن», or «نكص», or «شديد العقاب», or «اذكروا». «غرَّ هؤلاءِ دينَهم» is accusative in position as the object of the saying.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَتَوَفَّى الذين كَفَرُواْ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Aʿraj read «تتوفَّى» with the feminine tāʾ, because the group is feminine. The rest read it with the yāʾ of the third person, with two explanations. The more apparent is that it agrees with the reading of those before, in that the subject is the angels, and it is masculine only because of the separation, the feminine being figurative (majāzī). The second is that the subject is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, because He was mentioned before; «الملائكةُ» is then the mubtadaʾ and «يَضْربون» its khabar. On this reading there are two views on the sentence. One is that it is a ḥāl from the object. The second is that it is resumptive, an answer to an implied question; on this, one pauses at «الذين كفروا», unlike the two preceding views. Ibn ʿAṭiyya weakened the view of ḥāl because of the absence of the wāw, but it is not weak, given the frequency of a ḥāl clause containing a pronoun of the owner of the ḥāl and free of a wāw, in verse and prose. On the view that «الملائكة» is the subject, «يَضْربون» is a ḥāl clause, whether it is read with the feminine or the masculine. The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, being indicated, that is: "you would have seen a great thing."
His saying: {وَذُوقُواْ} is accusative by an implied saying of the angels, that is: "they strike them and say to them: taste." It was also said that the wāw in «يَضْربون» refers to the believers, that is: "they strike them during the fighting, and the angels strike them while taking their souls."
His saying: {وَأَنَّ الله} is conjoined to «ما» which is genitive by the bāʾ, that is: "that is because of what your hands have sent ahead, and because Allah is not unjust to the servants."

semin-durr:52-52.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {كَدَاْبِ آلِ}: Its like has already been given in Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying, the Exalted: {ذلك بِأَنَّ}: It is also a mubtadaʾ and khabar, like its counterpart, that is: "that punishment, or vengeance, is because Allah ..." As for His saying «وأنَّ الله سميعٌ», the majority read the fatḥa of «أنَّ», conjoined to the «أنَّ» before it, that is: "and the cause is that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." It is also read with kasra, as a resumption.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَدَأْبِ}: A group said: "It is a repetition of the first." Another group said: it is repeated not for emphasis, for several reasons, among them: that the first is a habit (daʾb) in that they were destroyed when they disbelieved, while this is a habit in that Allah did not change their blessing until they themselves changed it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. Among them: that the second proceeds as an elaboration of the first, for the first contains the mention of their crimes and the second the mention of their drowning; the first speaks of the punishment that comes down on them at the moment of death, and the second of the punishment that befalls them in the Hereafter; and in the first He used «بآيات الله», pointing to their denial of mentioning the proofs of divinity, while in the second He used «بآيات ربهم», pointing to their denial of the One who reared them and did good to them. Al-Kirmānī said: "It is possible that the pronoun in «كفروا» in the first verse refers to Quraysh, and the pronoun in «كذَّبوا» in the second refers to the House of Pharaoh and those mentioned with them."
His saying: {وَكُلٌّ كَانُواْ ظَالِمِينَ}: The pronoun in «كانوا» and «ظالمين» are put in the plural, in regard to the meaning of «كل»; for whenever «كلاً» is cut off from annexation, it is permissible to follow its form at one time and its meaning at another. The meaning was chosen here only for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil); had the form been followed, and it said for instance «وكلٌّ كان ظالماً», the endings would not agree.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying, the Exalted: {الذين عَاهَدْتَّ}: Several views are possible. The first: nominative as a badal from the relative noun before it, or as its adjective, or as ʿaṭf bayān; or accusative in the sense of blame (ʿalā l-dhamm); or nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being His saying «فإمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّ», in the sense: "whoever of them, that is of the disbelievers, makes a covenant and then breaks their covenant — if you gain the upper hand over them, do such-and-such." The fāʾ enters the khabar because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to a condition. This is the apparent sense of Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words. «منهم» may be a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun of the relative, the implied form being: "those with whom you made a covenant, i.e. being of them," so «مِنْ» is partitive. It was said that it means "with." It was said that the speech is carried by its meaning, that is: "you took a covenant from them." It was said that it is redundant, that is: "you made a covenant with them." The three views are weak and the first is the soundest.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَشَرِّدْ}: The majority read it with the undotted dāl. Tashrīd means driving away, scattering and making them heard of (tasmīʿ); all these meanings suit the verse. Al-Aʿmash, with a difference reported from him, read it with the dotted dhāl. The Shaykh said: "It is also so in the muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh." I say: it has already been mentioned that dotting and vocalisation are a later innovation, introduced by Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, so how could that be found in the muṣḥaf of Ibn Masʿūd? It was said: this root, I mean shīn, rāʾ, dotted dhāl, is unused in the language of the Arabs. There are several explanations of this reading. The first: the dhāl is a replacement through adjacency, as they say laḥm kharādīl and kharādhīl. The second: it is transposed from shadhar, from their saying "they scattered shadhar madhar," and from it comes al-shadhr, the gold found on the surface of the mine, because of its scatteredness. He said:
2433 - غرائِرُ في كِنٍّ وصَوْنٍ ونَعْمة ... يُحَلَّيْنَ ياقوتاً وشَذْراً مُفَقَّرا
(Unspoiled girls in shelter, protection and ease, adorned with rubies and with engraved nuggets of gold.)
The third: it is from "shadhara fī maqālihi" when one says much in it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and its meaning is unsuitable here. Quṭrub said: "sharadha with the dotted letter means exemplary punishment (tankīl), and with the undotted letter scattering," and this strengthens the view of those who said that this root is established in the language of the Arabs.
His saying: «مَنْ خَلْفَهم» is the object of «شَرِّد». Al-Aʿmash, with a difference reported from him, and Abū Ḥaywa read «مِنْ خلفِهم» as a preposition and its genitive noun. On this reading the object is omitted, that is: "scatter their like among the enemies, or people who act as they act." The two pronouns in «لعلهم يَذَّكَّرون» apparently refer to «مَنْ خلفهم», that is: when they see what befell the covenant-breakers, they will take heed. It was said that they refer to the covenant-breakers, but that has no substantial meaning.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فانبذ إِلَيْهِمْ}: Its object is omitted, that is: "cast back to them their covenants," that is: throw them away and pay them no heed. «على سواء» is a ḥāl, either from the subject, that is: "cast them while you are on a straight path," i.e. being on justice, so do not take them by surprise with fighting but inform them of it; or from the subject and the object together, that is: "both being on equality in knowledge or in enmity." The majority read with fatḥa on the sīn, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī with kasra, which is a dialect I have already pointed out at the beginning of al-Baqara.
His saying: {إِنَّ الله لاَ يُحِبُّ الخائنين}: This sentence may be a causal explanation, in meaning, of the command to cast back the covenant on equal terms, which is informing them; or it may be resumptive, brought to condemn whoever betrayed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and broke his covenant.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ}: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «يَحْسَبَنَّ» with the yāʾ of the third person here; and in al-Nūr, in His saying «لا يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كفروا معجزين [في الأرض]», likewise except for Ḥafṣ. The rest read with the tāʾ of address.
In the reading with the third person there are many explanations, whose like were given at the end of Āl ʿImrān. It is necessary to mention what will alert you here to what preceded. Among them: that the verb is attributed to a pronoun that the context explains, its implied form being: "and let him not think," i.e. the group of the believers, or the Messenger, or some reckoner; or the pronoun may refer to «مَنْ خلفهم». On these views «الذين كفروا» may be the first object, and «سبقوا» a sentence in the position of accusative as the second object. It was also said that the verb is attributed to «الذين كفروا», and then these scholars differed over the two objects. One group said: the first is omitted, its implied form being: "let those who disbelieve not think them to have outstripped," so «هم» is the first object and «سَبَقوا» is in the position of the second; or the implied form is: "let those who disbelieve not think themselves to have outstripped," which is in meaning like the preceding. Another group said: rather, the relative «أن» is omitted, and it and what is within its scope stands in place of the two objects, the implied form being: "let those who disbelieve not think that they have outstripped," the relative «أن» being omitted while its ṣila remains, as in His saying {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ} [al-Rūm: 24], i.e. «أن يريكم», and their saying «تَسْمَعُ بالمُعَيْدِيِّ خيرٌ من أن تراه» ("that you hear of al-Muʿaydī is better than that you see him"), and his saying:
2434 - ألا أيُّهذا الزاجري أحضرُ الوغى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who forbid me to attend the battle ...)
What supports this view is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «أنهم سبقوا». Another group said: rather, «سبقوا» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, and what stands in place of the two objects is «أنهم لا يعجزون», in the reading of whoever read «أنهم» with fatḥa, who is Ibn ʿĀmir; the implied form is: "let those who disbelieve not think, having outstripped, that they cannot be made powerless," and «لا» is redundant so that the meaning is sound.
Al-Zamakhsharī, after mentioning these views, said: "This reading, in which Ḥamza alone is singular, is not luminous." A group rejected this statement of his and said: Ḥamza was not alone in it; rather he was joined in it, among the Seven Readers, by Ibn ʿĀmir, the eldest of the readers and the highest in chain of transmission, and by ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ; then it is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī, the teacher of Nāfiʿ, and of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, Ibn Muḥayṣin, ʿĪsā, al-Aʿmash, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Abū Rajāʾ, Ṭalḥa and Ibn Abī Laylā. The Shaykh also rejected his statement that «لا يحسبَنَّ» falls on «أنهم لا يُعْجِزون» with «لا» as an addition, because that cannot work with the reading of Ḥamza, for Ḥamza reads with kasra on the hamza; that is: how can Ḥamza's reading fit this explanation? I say: he did not commit himself to explaining it according to Ḥamza's reading in both places — I mean «لا يَحْسَبَنَّ» and their saying «أنهم لا يعجزون» — so that we should hold him to what was mentioned.
As for the reading with the tāʾ of address, it is clear, that is: "do not think, O Muḥammad," or "O hearer"; «الذين كفروا» is the first object and the second is «سبقوا». It had been mentioned in Āl ʿImrān that the subject may be the relative noun, and that he used the feminine tāʾ because it has the meaning of "people," as in {كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 105], and a discussion of it was given there, which applies here.
As for the reading of the rest in al-Nūr, it admits what was mentioned here except the view in which the relative «أن» is supposed, because that is impossible; but another view takes its place, which cannot work here: that «الذين كفروا» is the subject, «مُعْجزين» the first object and «في الأرض» the second, that is: "do not think anyone can frustrate Allah on earth," i.e. by his strength. The reading with address is clear as I have set out for you.
Al-Aʿmash read «ولا يَحْسَبَ الذين كفروا» with fatḥa on the bāʾ. Its explanation is that the verb is emphasised by the light nūn of emphasis, which he omitted because of the meeting of two sākins, as the tanwīn is omitted for it; so it is like the saying of the other:
2435 - لا تُهينَ الفقير عَلَّكَ أَنْ تَرْ ... كَعَ يوماً والدهرُ قد رفعهْ
(Do not humiliate the poor man; perhaps you may one day be brought low while Fortune has raised him.)
that is: «لا تهينَنَّ». Some reported: «ولا تحسَبِ الذين» without any emphasis at all. This reading is with kasra on the bāʾ, on the basis of the meeting of two sākins.
Their saying: {إِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُعْجِزُونَ}: Ibn ʿĀmir read with fatḥa, the rest with kasra. The fatḥa is either on the omission of the causal lām, that is: "because they ..." Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim found Ibn ʿĀmir's reading remote. The reason for finding it remote is that it is a justification of the prohibition, that is: "do not think them to have escaped because they cannot be made powerless," i.e. do not let a thought of theirs occur to you because they cannot be made powerless; or else it is a badal from the object of the thinking.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is attached to «تحسب»: either as an object or as a badal from «سَبَقوا», and on both views «لا» is redundant. This is weak for two reasons: one, the redundancy of «لا»; the other, that when the object of «حَسِب» is a sentence and is the second object, the «إنَّ» in it takes kasra because it is a place of mubtadaʾ and khabar."
His saying: {لاَ يُعْجِزُونَ}: The majority read with one light nūn with fatḥa, which is the nūn of the nominative. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يُعْجِزوني» with a single nūn followed by the first-person yāʾ, which is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) or the nūn of the nominative. The disagreement about that has already been given in Sūrat al-Anʿām at {أتحاجواني}. Al-Zajjāj said: "The preferred is fatḥa on the nūn, and kasra is possible on the basis that the meaning is «لا يُعْجزونني», with the first nūn omitted because of the meeting of the two nūns, as ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
2436 - تراه كالثَّغام يُعَلُّ مِسْكاً ... يَسُوءُ الفالياتِ إذا فَلَيْني
(You see it like white thaghām scented with musk, vexing the women who delouse when they delouse me.)
and Mutammim ibn Nuwayra said:
2437 - ولقد عِلِمْتِ ولا محالةَ أنني ... للحادثات فهل تَرَيْني أجزعُ
(You know, without doubt, that I am [steadfast] before misfortunes; do you see me panic?)
Al-Akhfash said of this verse: "This is permissible out of necessity."
Ibn Muḥayṣin also read «يُعْجِزونِّ» with a doubled nūn with kasra, assimilating the nominative nūn into the protective nūn and omitting the yāʾ of the first person, content with the kasra in its place. From him also is fatḥa on the ʿayn, doubling of the jīm and kasra on the nūn, from ʿajjaza with doubling. Abū Jaʿfar said: "This is wrong for two reasons: one, that the meaning of ʿajjazahu is that he weakened him and weakened his affair; the other, that it should have been with two nūns." I say: as for al-Naḥḥās's judging it wrong, it is itself wrong, because bringing two nūns is not obligatory but permissible, and it was read so in places in the mutawātir readings, some of which will come. As for ʿajjaza with doubling, its meaning is not limited to what he mentioned; rather, others of the lexicographers reported that its meaning is "he ascribed me to incapacity," and that its meaning is "he delayed and hindered," and the reading's meaning suits one of the two meanings. Ṭalḥa read with kasra on the nūn, light.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّن قُوَّةٍ}: It is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, and its owner has two views. One is that it is the relative noun. The second is that it is its returning pronoun, since the implied form is: "what you are able to, being part of strength." «مِنْ» may also be for specifying the kind. As for «رباط», they allowed that it be the plural of rabṭ, the maṣdar of rabaṭa yarbuṭu, like kaʿb and kiʿāb, kalb and kilāb; or that it be a maṣdar of rabaṭa like ṣāḥa ṣiyāḥan — they said, because the maṣdars of the triliteral verb are not regular; or that it be the maṣdar of rābaṭa. The meaning of the reciprocal form is that the tying of horses is done by each for the other's doing, so the believers garrison against each other. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh said: "His saying 'the maṣdars of the unaugmented triliteral are not regular' is not correct; rather, they have regular maṣdars, which the grammarians mentioned." I say: there is a well-known disagreement in the matter, and he did not report a consensus on the absence of regularity so as to be refuted by the disagreement; he may have chosen one of the schools and held it, and he cannot be refuted by the other view. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-ribāṭ is a name for the horses that are tied in the cause of Allah. It may be named by al-ribāṭ in the sense of al-murābaṭa (garrisoning), and it may be the plural of rabīṭ, meaning marbūṭ (tied), like faṣīl and fiṣāl." The maṣdar here is annexed to its object.
His saying: «تُرْهبون» may be a ḥāl from the subject of «أعِدُّوا», that is: "prepare this for them while you are terrifying," or a ḥāl from its object, which is the relative noun, that is: "prepare it as something to terrify with." It may be attributed to each of them because the sentence contains the pronouns of both. This is if we make the pronoun in «به» refer to the relative «ما». But if we make it refer to the preparing indicated by «أعِدُّوا», or to al-ribāṭ, or to al-quwwa interpreted as might (ḥawl), it cannot be a ḥāl from the relative noun. It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of «لهم»; so the Shaykh reported from others, saying: "«وتُرْهبون»: they said, a ḥāl from the pronoun of «أعِدُّوا» or from the pronoun of «لهم»," and he did not follow it with objection. But how can it be correct to make it a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لهم» when there is no link between them? And it is not correct to supply a pronoun in the sentence «تُرْهبون» since it has taken its object.
Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb read, and Ibn ʿAqīl transmitted it from Abū ʿAmr, «تُرَهِّبون» with doubling, making it transitive by doubling as the majority made it transitive by the hamza. The second object in both readings is omitted, because the verb before the transfer by hamza or doubling is transitive to one, like rahhabtuka; the implied form is: "you terrify the enemy of Allah with fighting you or meeting you." Abū Ḥātim claimed that Abū ʿAmr reported the reading of al-Ḥasan with the yāʾ of the third person and light «يُرْهبون»; it is a clear reading, for the pronoun then refers to what the pronoun of «لهم» refers to, for if they are afraid they terrify those behind them.
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywa and Mālik ibn Dīnār read «ومن رُبُط» with two ḍammas, and from al-Ḥasan also rubṭ with ḍamma and sukūn, like kitāb and kutub. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In making it a plural, it being a maṣdar whose kinds do not differ, there is something to consider." I say: we do not concede, in that case, that it is a maṣdar; rather, Abū Zayd reported that «رِباطاً» is five horses and upwards, and that its plural is «رُبُط». And even if it were conceded to be a maṣdar, we do not concede that its kinds do not differ. It has already been mentioned that «رباطاً» may be the plural of the maṣdar rabṭ, so whatever was the answer there is the answer here.
His saying: {عَدْوَّ الله}: The majority read it annexed. Al-Sulamī read it with tanwīn and «لله» with the genitive lām, and it is singular, the genus being meant, so its meaning is "enemies of Allah." The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "He made it indefinite with the meaning of the generality, because it is also indefinite, not made definite by annexation to a definite, because the active participle has the meaning of present or future, and that does not become definite even if annexed to definites. As for «وعدوَّكم», it may be likewise indefinite, or it may become definite because its mention is repeated, and similarly: 'I saw a companion of yours, and your companion said to me.'" He means that «عدواً» may be taken with the sense of a description, so that it does not become definite, or not taken so, so that it becomes definite.
His saying: {وَآخَرِينَ} is conjoined to «عدو الله», and «من دونهم» is an adjective of «آخرين». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«من دونهم» is in the position of your saying 'other than these being [so]'; «دون» in the speech of the Arabs and «من دون» imply the absence of what is mentioned after them from the situation in which the saying occurs; from it is the proverb: «وأُمِرَّ دون عُبَيْدَةَ الوَذَمُ»." He means that the adverbiality here is figurative, because «دون» must be an adverbial, either literally or figuratively.
His saying: {لاَ تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ الله يَعْلَمُهُمْ}: There are two views on this verse. The first is that «علم» here takes one object, because it has the meaning of "to know, be acquainted with" (ʿarafa), and for that reason it takes one. The second is that it is in its ordinary sense and takes two, the second being omitted, that is: "you do not know them to be fighters or warring." One thing needs to be pointed out here: these two views cannot both apply to His saying «الله يَعْلمهم»; rather it must be said that it is the one taking two objects, with the second omitted, because of the difference you have already learned between ʿilm and maʿrifa. Among them: that maʿrifa requires prior ignorance; and among them: that its object is essences rather than relations; and the scholars have stated explicitly that it is not permissible to apply that, I mean the predication of maʿrifa, to Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن جَنَحُواْ}: Al-junūḥ is inclining. Janaḥat al-ibil: the camels bent their necks. Dhū l-Rumma said:
2438 - إذا ماتَ فوق الرَّحْلِ أَحْيَيْتُ روحَه ... بذكراكِ والعِيسُ المَراسِيلُ جُنَّحُ
(When he [the rider] drooped, almost dead, upon the saddle, I revived his spirit with the thought of you, while the swift white camels leaned forward.)
One says: janaḥa l-layl: night approached. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "Janaḥa l-rajul ilā fulān and li-fulān: when he submitted to him." Al-junūḥ is also following, because it contains inclination. Al-Nābigha said, describing birds that follow an army:
2439 - جَوانحَ قد أيقَنَّ أنَّ قبيلَه ... إذا ما التقى الجمعانِ أولُ غالبِ
(Birds leaning forward, certain that his tribe, when the two armies meet, is the first to prevail.)
From it comes al-jawāniḥ for the ribs, because of their inclining over the contents of the body, and al-janāḥ (wing) from it, for its inclining on the bird. Some discussion of this root has already been given in al-Baqara, and of «السِّلم».
Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read here with kasra on the sīn, and likewise in Sūrat al-Qitāl {وتدعوا إِلَى السلم}. Ḥamza agreed with him on what is in al-Qitāl. «للسِّلْم» is attached to «جَنَحوا»; it was said that it is made transitive by it and by «إلى». It was said that here it has the meaning of «إلى». Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read «فاجنُحْ» with ḍamma on the nūn, which is the dialect of Qays, while the fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm. The pronoun in «لها» refers to «السلم», because it is both masculine and feminine. From its use as feminine is his saying:
2440 - وأَقْنَيْتُ للحربِ آلاتِها ... وأَعْدَدْتُ للسِّلْم أوزارَها
(I acquired for war its instruments, and I prepared for peace its burdens.)
and another said:
2441 - السِّلْمُ تأخذ منها ما رَضِيْتَ به ... والحربُ يَكْفيك من أنفاسها جُرَعُ
(Peace: you take of it what you are content with; war: sips of its breaths suffice you.)

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَنِ اتبعك}: There are several views. The first is that «مَنْ» is nominative in position, conjoined to the divine Name, that is: "Allah suffices you, and the believers." Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and a group explained it so, and it is the apparent view; there is no objection to it in respect of meaning, although some people found it hard that the believers should be sufficient for the Prophet ﷺ, and interpreted the verse as we shall mention.
The second is that «مَنْ» is genitive in position, conjoined to the kāf in «حَسْبُك», which is the view of the Kufans; al-Shaʿbī and Ibn Zayd explained it so, saying that the meaning is: "and the sufficiency of whoever follows you." The third is that its position is accusative as accompaniment (maʿiyya). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ومَن اتبعك»: the wāw has the meaning of «مع», and what follows it is accusative. You say «حَسْبُك وزيداً درهمٌ» and do not put it in the genitive, because conjoining an overt genitive noun to a pronoun is impossible." And he said:
2442 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَحَسْبَكَ والضحاكَ سيفٌ مُهَنَّدُ
(... A sword of Indian steel suffices you and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.)
"The meaning is: [Allah] suffices you and suffices your followers, the believers, as a helper." The Shaykh said: "This contradicts Sībawayh's statement, for he said: «حَسْبُك وزيداً درهمٌ»: since it has the meaning of «كفاك», and it was bad to carry it on the pronoun, they intended a verb, as if he said: «بحسبك ويُحْسِب أخاك [درهمٌ]»." Then he said: "In that implied verb is a pronoun referring to the dirham, and the intention with the dirham is fronting, so it belongs to the conjunction of sentences. It may not belong to the chapter of iʿmāl (competing governance), because the mubtadaʾ's demanding its khabar and governing it is not of the kind of a verb's demanding or what takes its place, nor of its governance, so that is not to be imagined in it." I say: al-Zajjāj preceded al-Zamakhsharī in making it an object of accompaniment, except that he made «حسب» a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), for he said: "Ḥasb is an ism fiʿl, the kāf is accusative, and the wāw has the meaning of «مع»." On this basis «اللهُ» is the subject, and on this supposition «ومَنْ» may be conjoined to the kāf, because it is an object of the ism fiʿl, not a genitive, for an ism fiʿl is not annexed. Then the Shaykh said: "But al-Zajjāj's school is wrong, because operators enter upon «حَسْب», as in «بحَسْبك درهم», and the Exalted said {فَإِنَّ حَسْبَكَ الله} [al-Anfāl: 62]; it is not established anywhere that it is an ism fiʿl so that this could be carried over to it."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya, after reporting from al-Shaʿbī and Ibn Zayd the meaning I gave from them, said: "In this interpretation «مَنْ» is accusative in position, conjoined to the position of the kāf, because its position is accusative in meaning, by «يكفيك», in whose place «حَسبك» stands." The Shaykh said: "This is not good, because «حَسْبك» is not among those in which the kāf is in the position of accusative; rather, this is a proper annexation, not from accusative; and «حسبك» is a mubtadaʾ annexed to the pronoun, and is neither a maṣdar nor an active participle, unless it is said to be conjoined by imagining (ʿaṭf ʿalā l-tawahhum), as if he imagined it had been said «يكفيك الله» or «كفاك الله»; but conjunction by imagining is not regular. What should be carried over to the words of al-Shaʿbī and Ibn Zayd is that «مَنْ» is genitive by an omitted «حَسْب», indicated by «حَسْبك», like his saying: 2443 - أكلَّ امرئ تحسبين أمرأً ... ونارٍ توقَّدُ بالليل ناراً (Do you count every man a man, and every fire kindled at night a fire?), that is: «وكلَّ نارٍ», so it is not conjunction to the genitive pronoun." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This view, from omission of the muḍāf, is disliked; its chapter is poetic necessity." The Shaykh said: "It is neither disliked nor a necessity; Sībawayh allowed it and explained the verse and other speech by it." I say: his saying "rather, a proper annexation, not from accusative" is open to objection, because the grammarians hold that the annexation of «حسب» and its sisters is a non-genuine annexation (ghayr maḥḍa), and they justified that by saying that it is equivalent to an active participle governing a direct object, for «حَسْبك» means «كافيك», and «غيرك» means «مُغايرك», and «قيد الأوابد» means «مقيِّدها». They said: what indicates that is that indefinites are described by it, so it is said: «مررت برجلٍ حَسْبِك من رجلٍ».
Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed the nominative in three ways. The first: that it is conjoined to the divine Name, as mentioned earlier, except that he said: "so it is another khabar, like your saying «القائمان زيد وعمرو»", and «حَسْبك» is not put in the dual because it is a maṣdar. A group said: this is weak, because the wāw is for combining and it is not good here, as it is not good in their saying «ما شاء الله وشئت», where «ثم» is better here. I say: he means that, as a matter of etiquette, one does not bring the wāw which implies combining, but brings «ثم» which implies a delay, and the ḥadīth indicates that. The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and the sufficiency of whoever follows you." The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "and whoever follows you, likewise," that is: "Allah is sufficient for them."
Al-Shaʿbī read «ومَنْ» with sukūn on the nūn and «أَتْبَعَك» on the pattern of «أَكْرمك».

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {حَرِّضِ}: That is, urge and exhort. One says ḥarraḍa, ḥarrasha and ḥarraka with one meaning. Al-Harawī said: "One says ḥāraḍa ʿalā l-amr, akabba, wākaba, wāẓaba and wāṣaba with one meaning." It was said that its origin is from al-ḥaraḍ, which is destruction. He said:
2444 - إني امرؤ رابني همٌّ فأَحْرَضني ... حتى بُلِيْتُ وحتى شفَّني سَقَم
(I am a man whom a worry troubled and brought to ruin, until I was worn out and illness emaciated me.)
Abū Isḥāq said: "The sense of taḥrīḍ in the language is that a person is urged on something until it is known of him that he is ḥāriḍ, and the ḥāriḍ is the one close to perishing." People found this remote from him. Al-Zamakhsharī took the same course, saying: "Al-taḥrīḍ is exaggeration in urging a matter, from al-ḥaraḍ, which is that illness wears him out and presses upon him until he is on the verge of death, or you call him ḥaraḍ and say 'I see you only as ḥaraḍ.'"
His saying: {إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ} and the verses: He included a restriction in the first condition, namely patience, and omitted it from the second; and included in the second a restriction, namely their being of the disbelievers, and omitted it from the first. The implied form is: "two hundred of those who disbelieved, and a hundred patient"; so from each He omitted what He included in the other, and this is the height of eloquence.
The Kufans read {وإن يكنْ منكم مئة يَغْلبوا} {فإن يكنْ منكم مئة صابرة} with the masculine «يكن» in both. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read the feminine in both. Abū ʿAmr read the first like the Kufans and the second like the rest. Whoever used the masculine did so because of the separation between the verb and its subject by «منكم», and because the feminine is figurative, since the hundred means males. Whoever used the feminine did so on account of the separation, paying no heed to the meaning or to the separation. As for Abū ʿAmr, he distinguished between the two places, using the masculine in the first for what was mentioned, and because he noticed His saying «يَغْلبوا», and the feminine in the second for the strength of the feminine through its description by a feminine in His saying «صابرة».
As for «إنْ يكنْ منكم عشرون» and «وإن يكنْ منكم أَلْفٌ», it is masculine according to all the readers except al-Aʿraj, who made feminine the verb attributed to «عشرون».
Al-Aʿmash read «حَرِّصْ» with the undotted ṣād, from al-ḥirṣ (eagerness), whose meaning is close to the reading of the majority. Al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim read «وعُلِم» in the passive, and «أن فيكم ضعفاً» is in the position of nominative as standing in place of the agent, whereas in the reading of the majority it is in the position of accusative as direct object, because the subject of the verb is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted. «يكن» in these places may be the complete verb (tāmma), so «منكم» is either a ḥāl from «عشرون», because it was originally an adjective of it, or attached to the verb itself, since it is complete; or it may be the incomplete verb (nāqiṣa), so «منكم» is the khabar and the nominative is the ism, namely «عشرون», «مئة» and «ألف».
His saying: «ضعفاً»: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read here, and in al-Rūm in its three words {اللهُ الذي خَلَقكم مِنْ ضعف، ثم جَعَل من بعد ضعفٍ قوة، ثم جَعَلَ من بعد قوةٍ ضعفاً}, with fatḥa on the ḍād; the rest read with ḍamma. From Ḥafṣ alone there is a difference in al-Rūm specifically.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «ضُعُفاً» with ḍamma on both the fāʾ and the ʿayn; all are maṣdars. It was said: al-ḍaʿf with fatḥa is in opinion and intellect, and with ḍamma in the body; this is the view of al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad, as al-Rāghib reported it from him. When Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported this from al-Thaʿālibī, he said: "This view is refuted by the reading." It was also said that they are the same, two dialectal forms: the Hijazi form is the ḍamma and the Tamīmī form the fatḥa; Abū ʿAmr reported it, so they are like al-faqr and al-fuqr, al-makth and al-mukth, al-bukhl and al-bakhal. Ibn ʿAbbās read, as al-Naqqāsh and Abū Jaʿfar reported from him, «ضُعَفاء», a plural on the pattern fuʿalāʾ like ẓarīf and ẓurafāʾ. I have reported much from the readers concerning this word in the commentary on «Ḥirz al-Amānī», which suits it better than this place, so refer to it.

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ أسرى}: Abū ʿAmr read «تكون» with the feminine, regarding the meaning of a group; the rest read with the masculine, regarding the form of the plural. The majority here read «أَسْرى», which is the regular plural of faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, showing that it is like jarīḥ and jarḥā. Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim read «أُسَارى»; they likened «أسير» to kaslān and pluralised it on fuʿālā like kusālā, as they likened kaslān to it and pluralised it on kaslā. The discussion of both has already been given thoroughly in al-Baqara.
His saying: {يُثْخِنَ}: The majority read «يُثْخن» light, making it transitive by the hamza. Abū Jaʿfar, Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «يُثَخِّن» with doubling, making it transitive by doubling. It is derived from thakhāna, which is thickness and density in bodies, then it is borrowed for much killing and wounding. One says athkhanathu l-jirāḥ, that is: they weighed him down until they fixed him in place; from it {حتى إِذَآ أَثْخَنتُمُوهُمْ} [Muḥammad: 4]. It was said: "until you subdue." Al-ithkhān is subduing. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited:
