2445 - تُصَلِّي الضُّحى ما دهرُها بتعبُّدٍ ... وقد أَثْخَنَتْ فرعونَ في كفره كفرا
(She prays the forenoon prayer, not in her lifetime out of devotion, and she had weighed down Pharaoh in his disbelief with disbelief.)
Thus al-Harawī recited it as evidence for subduing, but there is no [clear] meaning in it, since the meaning rests on increase and exaggeration suited to its original meaning, which is thickness. From it one says thakhuna yathkhunu thakhānatan, so he is thakhīn, like ẓarufa yaẓrufu ẓarāfatan, so he is ẓarīf.
[Translator's note: the verse and the remark that "there is no meaning in it" are translated as written; the verse is obscure.]
His saying: {والله يُرِيدُ الآخرة}: The majority read «الآخرة» in the accusative; Sulaymān ibn Jammāz al-Madanī read it in the genitive, which is explained by the omission of the muḍāf and leaving the muḍāf ilayhi in the genitive. Some supplied: "the goods (ʿaraḍ) of the Hereafter," and this was faulted, since it is not good to say "Allah wants the goods of the Hereafter"; so al-Zamakhsharī amended it by making it so for the sake of contrast, saying "meaning its reward." Some supplied "deeds" or "reward." Abū l-Baqāʾ made it like the saying of the other:
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ونارٍ تَوَقَّدُ بالليلِ نارا
(... and every fire kindled at night, a fire.)
and supplied the muḍāf "ʿaraḍ of the Hereafter." The Shaykh said: "The verse is not like the line, for that is allowed when nothing separates the conjunction from the genitive noun, as in the line, or it is separated by «لا», as in «ما مثل زيد ولا أخيه يقولان ذلك»; but when it is separated by anything else, as in this reading, it is irregular and rare."

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ}: «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, the maṣdar standing in the place of the object. It may also mean "that which" (alladhī), which in meaning is like the former, and the returning pronoun on this view is omitted.
His saying: {حَلاَلاً} is accusative as ḥāl, either from the relative «ما» or from its returning pronoun if we make it a noun. It was also said that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "lawful eating."
His saying: {واتقوا الله}: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His saying «واتقوا الله» came as an eloquent parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ) in the middle of the speech, because His saying {إِنَّ الله غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ} is connected to His saying {فَكُلُواْ مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ}." He means that it is connected to it in that it is like its reason.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنَ الأسرى}: Abū ʿAmr read it on the pattern fuʿālā, and the rest on the pattern faʿlā; what is in both is already known. Qatāda, Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū Jaʿfar agreed with Abū ʿAmr. There was a difference reported from al-Jaḥdarī and al-Ḥasan. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «مِنْ أَسْرى» indefinite.
His saying: {يُؤْتِكُمْ} is the apodosis of the condition. Al-Aʿmash read «يُثِبْكم», from thawāb (reward). Al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywa, Shayba and Ḥumayd read «ممَّا أَخَذَ» in the active, the subject being Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:71-71.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن يُرِيدُواْ}: The pronoun refers to the captives, because they are the nearest thing mentioned. It was said: to those inclining (al-jāniḥīn). It was said: to the Jews. It was said: to the disbelievers of Quraysh.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَعَلَيْكُمُ النصر}: It is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, or, according to al-Akhfash, a verb and subject; the word «على» gives a sense of obligation. Al-Zamakhsharī likewise supplied it and compared it to the saying:
2446 - على مُكْثريهم رِزْقُ مَنْ يَعْتريهم ... وعند المُقِلِّين السماحةُ والبَذْلُ
(Upon their wealthy is the provision of whoever comes to them, and with the poor are generosity and giving.)
His saying: {مِّن وَلاَيَتِهِم}: Ḥamza read here, and in al-Kahf [verse 44] {الولاية لِلَّهِ}, he and al-Kisāʾī, with kasra on the wāw. The rest read with fatḥa. It was said that they are two dialectal forms. It was said: with fatḥa it is from al-mawlā (one says: a mawlā of clear walāya), and with kasra from the authority (wilāya) of the ruler; Abū ʿUbayda said this. It was said: with fatḥa it is from help and kinship, and with kasra from rule; al-Zajjāj said this. He said: "The kasra is possible because in the mutual taking of one another as allies by some of the people there is a kind of craft and work, and everything of the kind of craft takes kasra, like al-khiyāṭa and al-qiṣāra." Al-Aṣmaʿī judged the reading with kasra wrong, but he is the one in error, given that it is mutawātir.
Abū ʿUbayd said: "What we hold is to take the fatḥa in these two places, because their meaning is from alliance (muwālāt) in religion." Al-Fārisī said: "The fatḥa is better because it concerns religion." Al-Farrāʾ reversed this, saying: "He means 'from their inheritances' [translator: i.e. mīrāthihim]; with kasra on the wāw is dearer to me than the fatḥa, because it takes fatḥa only when it is help. Al-Kisāʾī took the fatḥa to mean help; yet both the fatḥa and the kasra have been heard in both meanings." Al-Sulamī and al-Aʿraj read «والله بما يعملون» with the yāʾ of the third person, as though it were a shift of person (iltifāt) or a report about them.
[Translator's note: the passage attributed to al-Farrāʾ is garbled in the source («يُريد مِنْ مواريثهم»); it is translated as it stands.]

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِنْ لا تَفْعَلُوهُ}: The hāʾ refers either to the help, or the inheritance, or the covenant (that is, keeping it), or to everything mentioned before; that is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's saying "if you do not do what I have commanded you." The majority read [«كبير»] with the single-dotted bāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī, as Abū Mūsā al-Ḥijāzī reported from him, read «كثير» with the three-dotted thāʾ, which is close to what is in al-Baqara, where he reads it so.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين آمَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ}: Some claimed that this sentence is a repetition of the one before it, but it is not so; the one before contained the mutual alliance of some of them with others, the division of the believers into three categories, and the statement of their ruling in their alliance and mutual help; whereas this contains praise, honouring and distinction, and what their state came to in terms of forgiveness and generous provision.
His saying «في كتاب» may be attached to «أَوْلَى» itself, that is: "more entitled in Allah's ruling, or in the Qur'an, or in the Preserved Tablet"; or it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "this ruling is mentioned in a book." How excellent is the way its conclusion was brought with His saying: {بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ}.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الأنفال}: the subject of «يَسْأل» refers back to a known group, namely those who were present at Badr. The verb «سأل» is sometimes used for requesting a meaning that lies in the person asked itself, and then it is made transitive by «عن», like this verse and like the poet's saying:

2379 - سَلي إنْ جَهِلْتِ الناسَ عنَّا وعنهمُ ... فليس سواءً عالمٌ وجَهولُ
(Ask, if you do not know, the people about us and about them; for the knowing and the ignorant are not equal.)

It may also be for requesting property and the like, and then it takes two objects, such as «سألت زيداً مالاً» (I asked Zayd for money). Some claimed that the asking here is in this sense and that «عن» is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being «يسألونك الأنفالَ»; and he supported his view with the reading of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, his son Zayd, his son Muḥammad al-Bāqir, his son Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq, ʿIkrima and ʿAṭāʾ: «يسألونك الأنفالَ» without «عن». The sound view is that this reading is on the intention of the preposition (omitted). Some said: «عن» is in the sense of «مِنْ»; and nothing calls for that.

Ibn Muḥayṣin read «عَلَّنْفَال». The origin is that he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the lām of definiteness, then took the incidental vowel into account and assimilated the nūn into the lām, as in {وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 38]; this has preceded in His saying {عَنِ الأهلة} [al-Baqara: 189].

Al-anfāl is the plural of nafal, which is an addition to the obligatory thing; the booty was called nafal because of its addition to the protection of the territory. Labīd said:

2380 - إنَّ تقوى ربِّنا خيرُ نَفَلْ ... وبإذنِ الله رَيْثي وعَجَلْ
(The fear of our Lord is the best of increase, and by Allah's permission are my delay and my haste.)

Another said:

2381 - إنَّا إذا احْمَرَّ الوغَى نَرْوي القَنا ... ونَعِفُّ عند مَقاسِمِ الأنفالِ
(When the battle reddens, we water the lances, and we are abstinent at the dividing of the spoils.)

It was also said: they were called «الأَنْفال» because the Muslims were favoured by them over the rest of the nations. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-nafal is what the raider is granted as an extra, i.e. given in addition to his share of the booty."

His saying: {ذَاتَ بِيْنِكُمْ}: the discussion of «ذات» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān. Here it is an adjective of an omitted direct object, the implied form being: "and set right the conditions of your separation and of your union", or "the place connected with you", for it was said that «بين» here is meant as separation, or union, or the adverbial sense. Al-Zajjāj and others said: "«ذات» here is in the position of the reality of a thing and its self", and Ibn ʿAṭiyya made that clear. Explaining it by clarification of this is better.

The Shaykh said: "Al-bayn is separation, and «ذات» is an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. 'set right conditions pertaining to your separation'; when the conditions were closely connected with the bayn, their description was annexed to it, as you say «اسْقِني ذا إنائك», i.e. 'water, the one belonging to your vessel'; when the water was in contact with the vessel it was described by «ذا» and annexed to the vessel. The meaning: give me to drink what is in the vessel of water.'"

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَجِلَتْ}: one says wajila with kasra in the past, yawjalu with fatḥa; there is another minor dialectal form, read in the irregular readings: wajalat with fatḥa on the jīm in the past and kasra in the imperfect, so the wāw is dropped, like waʿada yaʿidu. In the well-known form one says wajila yawjalu. Some of them say yājalu, turning the wāw into alif, which is irregular because it is a conversion of the weak letter on one of two grounds only: the opening vowel of what precedes the weak letter, without its being vowelled; this is parallel to «طائي» in the nisba of ṭayyiʾ. Some of them say yījalu with kasra on the imperfect prefix, so the wāw turns into yāʾ because of its quiescence and the kasra of what precedes it. It has preceded at the beginning of this subject that some Arabs put kasra on the imperfect prefix under conditions, among them that the prefix not be yāʾ, except in this word and in abā yibā.

Some of them composed from these two dialects another one, which is fatḥa on the yāʾ and converting the wāw into yāʾ, saying yayjalu: they took the conversion of the wāw from those who put kasra on the imperfect prefix, and took the fatḥa on the yāʾ from the dialect of the majority.

And His saying {إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ}: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The apodosis of the preceding condition is in His saying «وأطيعوا»; this is the school of Sībawayh; while the school of al-Mubarrad is that the apodosis is omitted and delayed, his school being that the apodosis does not precede the condition." I say: what Abū [Muḥammad] mentioned has been reported by people to be otherwise: they report that is, the permissibility of preceding the apodosis of the condition before it, from the Kufans, Abū Zayd and Abū l-ʿAbbās; Allah knows best which is the more firmly established. It is possible that al-Mubarrad had two views, and likewise Sībawayh, so that each party transmitted one of the two views from each of them.

semin-durr:3-3.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يُقِيمُونَ}: it is permissible for this relative noun to be nominative as an adjective (naʿt) of the preceding relative noun, or as a badal (substitute), or as its explicative apposition (bayān); and to be accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment), which suggests praise. And His saying {وعلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ}: the fronting conveys restriction, i.e. upon Him and not upon anyone else. This sentence may have a grammatical position, namely the accusative as a ḥāl from the object of «زادَتْهم»; it may be resumptive; and it may be conjoined to the ṣila before it, thereby entering the sphere of the preceding ṣilas; and on these latter two possibilities it has no grammatical position.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {حَقّاً}: it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "they are the believers with true faith". It may be an emphasis (muʾakkid) of the content of the clause, as in your saying «هو عبد الله حقاً» (he is the servant of Allah, truly); the governor in it, on both views, is implied, i.e. "I affirm it truly". It may also, though very weakly, be an emphasis of the content of the clause occurring after it, namely «لهم درجات», the speech being complete at His saying «هم المؤمنون», then beginning with «حقاً لهم درجات». This is permissible only on a weak view, I mean the fronting of the emphasising maṣdar before the content of a clause it emphasises.

His saying: {عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ}: it may be attached to «درجات» because it is in the sense of «أُجُورٌ» (rewards); or attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «درجات», i.e. "established with their Lord"; or attached to what «لهم» is attached to, namely being established.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَآ أَخْرَجَكَ}: there are twenty possibilities in it. The first: the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being: "the spoils are established for Allah, an establishment like His bringing you out", i.e. an establishment in truth, like your being brought out from your house in truth, meaning that there is no doubt in that. The second: the implied form is: "and set right the conditions between you, a setting right like His bringing you out." He has shifted from addressing the group to addressing the individual. The third: the implied form is: "and obey Allah and His Messenger, an obedience verified and firm, like His bringing you out", i.e. as there is no doubt or ambiguity in Allah's bringing you out. The fourth: the implied form is: "they rely [on Allah] with a true reliance, like your Lord's bringing you out." The fifth: the implied form is: "they are the believers truly, as He brought you out", so it is an adjective of «حقاً».

The sixth: the implied form is: "ranks have been established for them, and likewise a firm establishment like the establishment of your being brought out." The seventh: that it is attached to what follows, the implied form being: "they dispute with you a disputation like your Lord's bringing you out." The eighth: the implied form is: "they are averse, a firm aversion, as your Lord brought you out", i.e. these two things, the disputing and the aversion, are certain without doubt, just as your being brought out is certain without doubt. The ninth: the kāf is in the sense of «إذ» and «ما» is added; the implied form: "Remember when He brought you out." This is utterly invalid, since nowhere has it been established that the kāf is in the sense of «إذ»; and moreover «ما» is added only in places of which this is not one.

The tenth: the kāf is in the sense of the oath wāw, and «ما» is in the sense of «الذي» (the One who), referring to a being with knowledge and sworn by, and it has referred to a being with knowledge in His saying {والسمآء وَمَا بَنَاهَا} [al-Shams: 5] and {وَمَا خَلَقَ الذكر والأنثى} [al-Layl: 3]; the implied form: "by the One who brought you out", and His saying «يجادلونك» would be the answer to the oath. This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda. People have rejected it altogether, saying he was weak in grammar: when was it established that the kāf is a particle of oath in the sense of wāw? Moreover «يجادلونك» cannot be an answer, because in the Basran school, when it is an affirmative imperfect two things are necessary in it: the lām and one of the two nūns, such as {لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُوناً} [Yūsuf: 32], and in the Kufan school either the lām or one of the two nūns; and «يجادلونك» is devoid of both.

The eleventh: the kāf is in the sense of «على» and «ما» in the sense of «الذي», the implied form being: "proceed upon that which brought you out." It is weak because it has never been established that the kāf is in the sense of «على» except in a place open to dispute, such as His saying {واذكروه كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 198], i.e. upon His guiding you. The twelfth: the kāf is in the position of the nominative, the implied form: "as your Lord brought you out, so fear Allah", as if it were a mubtadaʾ and khabar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This meaning was set up by this commentator, and it is not among the wording of the verse in any beginning or end."

The thirteenth: it is also in the position of the nominative, the implied form being: "they have ranks with their Lord, forgiveness and generous provision; this is a true promise, like His bringing you out." In this there is an omission of a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and had he stated them the comparison would not cohere and would not be good.

The fourteenth: it is also in the position of the nominative. The implied form: "and set right the conditions between you; that is better for you, as He brought you out", so the kāf is in reality an adjective of the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It is weak because of the long separation between His saying «وأَصْلِحوا» and His saying «كما أَخْرَجَك».

The fifteenth: it is also in the position of the nominative, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, and the meaning is: he compared the aversion of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to his going out from Medina, when they verified that Quraysh had gone out to defend Abū Sufyān and protect his caravan, with their aversion to the removal of the spoils from their hands and making them for Allah and His Messenger, who rules concerning them as He pleases. Al-Zamakhsharī chose this possibility and approved of it, saying: "The position of the kāf is nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: this state is like the state of your being brought out; meaning that their state in disliking what you saw of the granting of extra shares to the raiders is like their state in disliking their going out to war." This which al-Zamakhsharī approved is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya explained it in terms like the preceding wording, for al-Farrāʾ said: "This kāf compared this story, which is his being brought out from his house, with the preceding story, which is their asking about the spoils."

The sixteenth: it is an adjective of the khabar of a mubtadaʾ also, both mubtadaʾ and khabar having been omitted. The implied form: "your division of the spoils is a right, as your being brought out was a right." The seventeenth: that the comparison occurs between two bringing-outs, i.e. your Lord's bringing you out from your house, which is Mecca, while you disliked your going out, and the outcome of that bringing out was victory and triumph, like His bringing you out from Medina while some of the believers disliked it, the going out being followed by triumph, victory and good, as the first going out was followed by it.

The eighteenth: the kāf is attached to His saying «فاضربوا». The elaboration of this, according to the proponent of this possibility: the kāf is for comparison in a figurative manner, like a person saying to his servant: "As I returned you to my enemies and they found you weak, and you asked for reinforcement and I reinforced you, and removed your excuses, take them now and punish them; as I have been good to you and sent you provision, do such and such and thank me for it." So the implied form of the verse: "As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, and covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him, and sent down water upon you from the sky to purify you with it, and sent down upon you angels following one after another, so strike above the necks and strike from them every finger-tip." It is as if He were saying: "I have removed your excuses and reinforced you with the angels, so strike these places in them, which is killing, so that you may reach what Allah intends in establishing the truth and nullifying falsehood." This possibility, after its length, has no profit in it, because of its distance from the meaning and the many separations.

The nineteenth: the implied form is: "as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth", i.e. by reason of making the religion of Allah manifest and strengthening His law, while they disliked your going out, being in awe of fighting and fearing death — for he ﷺ was commanded to set out with them suddenly and they were not prepared to go out — and they disputed with you about the truth after it had become clear: Allah gave you victory and reinforced you with His angels; and the speech that follows indicates this omitted element, namely His saying {إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ} [al-Anfāl: 9] and the following verses. The Shaykh approved this possibility and claimed that he had not been preceded in it. Then he said: "It appears that the kāf is not for pure comparison but has the meaning of giving a reason. The grammarians have stated explicitly that it is for giving a reason, and derived on that His saying {واذكروه كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 198], and they recited:

2382 - لا تَشْتُمِ الناس كما لا تُشْتَمُ ... أي: لانتفاء شتم الناس لك لا تشتمهم
(Do not revile people, so that you will not be reviled — i.e. because of the absence of people's reviling you, do not revile them.)

and among common speech: «كما تطيع الله يدخلك الجنة», i.e. because of your obedience to Allah He will admit you; so likewise the verse, and the meaning: because you went out to strengthen the religion of Allah and to kill His enemies, He gave you victory and reinforced you with the angels."

The twentieth: the implied form: "and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers; as your going out was in obedience, it is better for you, just as your going out was better for them." These views, for all their number, are mostly weak, and I have made that clear. His saying: {بالحق}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: it is attached to the verb, i.e. by reason of the truth: it is a bringing out by reason of a truth that appears, namely the exaltation of the word of Islam and victory over the enemies of Allah. The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the object of «أَخْرَجَكَ», i.e. "accompanied by the truth".

His saying: {وَإِنَّ فَرِيقاً}: the wāw is for ḥāl, the clause is in the accusative position, and for this reason «إنَّ» was given kasra. The object of «كارهون» is omitted, i.e. "averse to going out"; the reason for the aversion is either the natural recoiling from what is anticipated of fighting, or lack of preparation.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُجَادِلُونَكَ}: it may be resumptive, informing of their state of disputing. It may be a second ḥāl, i.e. "He brought you out while they were disputing with you". It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكارهون», i.e. "averse while disputing". The apparent sense is that the nominative pronoun refers to the group mentioned earlier, and the meaning of the disputing is their saying: "How shall we fight when we have not prepared for fighting?" It may also refer to the disbelievers, whose disputing is obvious. His saying «بعدما تبيَّن» is governed by the disputing, and «ما» is infinitival (maṣdariyya), i.e. "after its becoming clear and evident", which is uglier than disputing about a thing before it becomes clear. ʿAbd Allāh read «بُيِّن» in the passive, from bayyantuhu, i.e. I made it manifest.

His saying: {وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ}: a ḥāl from the object of «يُساقُون».

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ}: «إذ» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "remember when". The majority read the dāl with ḍamma because it is an imperfect in the nominative. Muslim ibn Muḥārib read it with sukūn, as a lightening because of the succession of vowels. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يعدكم الله احدى» with the hamza of «إحدى» as a hamzat waṣl, as a lightening contrary to analogy; this parallels the reading of one who read «إنها لاحدى» with dropping of the hamza, treating the hamzat qaṭʿ as a hamzat waṣl. He also read «أحد» in the masculine, because «الطائفة» is feminine only figuratively (majāzī). Muslim ibn Muḥārib read «بكلمته» in the singular, the generic noun being meant, so it serves the function of the plural.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيُحِقَّ}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: it is attached to what precedes, i.e. "and He cuts off so that He may establish the truth". The second: it is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being: "He did that so that He might establish the truth", i.e. He did it only for these two things, namely establishing Islam, making it manifest, and the removal of disbelief and the like.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The omitted element must be supplied as delayed, so as to convey restriction and for the meaning to fit it." I say: this is according to his view, and it is the sound one.

His saying: {أَنَّها لكم}: it is accusative in position as a badal (substitute) from «إحدى», i.e. "He promises you that one of the two groups will be yours", i.e. you will have power over it as owners have power; so it is a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion).

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ}: there are five possibilities in it. The first: it is accusative by an implied «اذكر» (remember), for which reason al-Ḥawfī called it resumptive, i.e. cut off from what precedes. The second: it is accusative by «يحقُّ», i.e. "He establishes the truth at the time of your seeking help." This is the view of Ibn Jarīr. It is a mistake, because «ليحقَّ» is future, being accusative by an implied «أَنْ», while «إذ» is an adverb of past time; so how can the future govern the past? The third: it is a badal (substitute) from the first «إذ», as al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ said; they had already put forward that the governor of the first «إذ» is an implied «اذكر». The fourth: it is accusative by «يعدكم», as al-Ḥawfī said, and al-Ṭabarī before him. The fifth: it is accusative by His saying «تَوَدُّون», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said; and there is remoteness in it because of the long separation.

The verb «استغاث» is transitive by itself and with the bāʾ. In the Quran it has not occurred except transitive by itself, so that Ibn Mālik took exception to the grammarians' saying "al-mustaghāth lahu", or "bihi", or "min ajlihi". They recited, in support of its being transitive with a preposition, the poet's saying:

2383 - حتى استغاثَ بماءٍ لا رِشَاءَ له ... من الأباطحِ في حافَاتِه البُرَكُ
مُكَلَّلٌ بأصول النَّبْت تَنْسُجه ... ريحٌ خَرِيقٌ لضاحي مائِه حُبُكُ
كما استغاث بِسَيْءٍ فَزُّغَيْطَلَةٍ ... خافَ العيونَ ولم يُنْظَرْ به الحَشَكُ
(…until he sought relief in water with no rope to draw it, from the wadi-beds, with pools along its edges; crowned with the roots of plants, a strong wind weaving ripples on the exposed surface of its water; as the …-bird sought help …, fearing the eyes, and no milk-rush was awaited from it.)
[Translator's note: the third verse is obscure and corrupt in the source as printed; the gloss is tentative.]

This indicates that it is transitive with a preposition, as Sībawayh and others used it.

His saying: {أَنِّي}: the majority read the hamza with fatḥa, with an implied omission of the preposition, i.e. "so He responded with: I (am)". ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, and it is also reported from Abū ʿAmr, read «إني» with kasra. There are two schools on it: the Basran school that it is on the implication of a saying, i.e. "so He said: I am reinforcing you"; and the Kufan school that it is quoted by «استجاب», treating it as the saying, since it is in its meaning.

His saying: {بِأَلْفٍ}: the majority read the singular. Al-Jaḥdarī read «بآلُفٍ» on the pattern of afluṣ. From him also and from al-Suddī, on the pattern of aḥmāl. In reconciling these two readings with the majority reading: the majority reading is taken to mean that by "a thousand" the leaders are meant, the rest being like followers to them; for that reason they were not specified in the majority reading and were specified in these two. Or the thousand is taken to mean those of the angels who fought as opposed to those who did not fight; then there is no contradiction between the readings.

His saying: {مُرْدِفِينَ}: Nāfiʿ, and it is also reported from Qunbul, read «مُرْدَفين» with fatḥa on the dāl, and the rest with kasra. Both are clear, since it is reported in tafsīr that behind every angel was an angel riding behind him. The fatḥa reading suggests that others made them ride behind, by their riding behind them; and the kasra reading suggests that the one riding behind his companion made him ride behind (arkaba-hu). So the expression is sound with the active participle at times and the passive participle at others. Abū l-Baqāʾ made the object of «مُرْدِفين», meaning with kasra, omitted, i.e. "causing others like themselves to ride behind". He also allowed that the meaning of irdāf is coming after the first ones, i.e. "they were made followers (ridf) to the first ones".

An answer is sought on how to reconcile this verse with the verse of Āl ʿImrān, where He said there «بخمسة» (with five) and said here «بأَلْف» (with a thousand), the story being one. The answer: this thousand is following upon those five, so the total is six thousand; and this appears and is strengthened in the reading «مُرْدِفين» with kasra on the dāl.

Abū ʿUbayd denied that the angels made one another ride behind, i.e. mounted other angels behind them. Al-Fārisī said: "Whoever puts kasra on the dāl, two possibilities arise: the first, that they are causing others like themselves to ride behind, as you say «أَرْدَفْتُ زيداً دابَّتي» (I made Zayd ride behind me on my mount), so the second object is omitted, and omission of the object is frequent. The other possibility: that they came after the Muslims. Al-Akhfash said: «بنو فلان يَرْدِفوننا», i.e. 'they come after us'; and Abū ʿUbayda said: 'murdifīn: they came afterwards; radifanī and ardafanī are one.'" Al-Fārisī said: "This possibility is seemingly clearer in view of His saying {إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ}: His saying «مُرْدِفين» means coming afterwards upon your seeking help. And whoever puts fatḥa on the dāl, they are murdafūn in the sense of: they were made to follow the people, i.e. sent down after them."

Some of the Meccans, as reported by al-Khalīl, read «مُرَدِّفين» with fatḥa on the rāʾ and a kasra'd doubled dāl, the origin being murtadifīn, which was assimilated. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "This reading is taken from raddafa with shaddah on the dāl for intensification, the doubling being a substitute for the hamza, like afraḥtuhu and farraḥtuhu." Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad allowed ḍamma on the rāʾ as a following of the ḍamma of the mīm, like their saying mukhuḍim with ḍamma on the khāʾ, and it was read thus irregularly.

«مُرِدِّفين» was also read, with kasra on the rāʾ and a kasra'd doubled dāl. The kasra on the rāʾ admits two explanations: either the meeting of two quiescent letters, or following. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "On this reading kasra on the mīm is possible, as a following of the rāʾ, but I do not remember it as a reading." I say: likewise the fatḥa in «مُرَدِّفين» in the reading which al-Khalīl reported admits two explanations. The first, and it is the apparent one, is that it is a vowel of transfer from the tāʾ when its assimilation into the rāʾ was intended. The second: that it was given fatḥa for lightness, although the origin is kasra by the rule of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as it has been read. «مِرْدِفين» was also read, with kasra on the mīm as a following of the kasra of the rāʾ.

Al-wajal is fright. It was also said: the feeling of fear. One says of it wajila, yawjalu, yājalu, yayjalu, yījalu, wajalan, and he is wajil. Al-shawka is weaponry, like the spearhead, the blade and the sword; its origin is from the plant with a sharp tip, like the thorn of the saʿdān; one says of it "a man shāʾik", the hamza being from a wāw like qāʾim, and it may be inverted by moving its ʿayn after its lām, so one says shākin, becoming like ghāzin, its pattern then being fāl. Zuhayr said:

2384 - لدى أسدٍ شاكي السِّلاحِ مُقَذَّفٍ ... له لِبَدٌ أظفارُه لم تُقَلَّمِ
(Near a lion, armed with weapons, solid-bodied, with a thick mane, his claws never pared.)

Weapons are described as shākin as a man is described by it, so one says rajulun shākin and shākin, and silāḥun shākin and shākin. As for shāk, it is sound, not weak, its alif being converted from the middle letter of the word, and its pattern originally faʿil with kasra on the ʿayn, but it was turned into alif, as they said "kabsh ṣāf", i.e. ṣawif (woolly); and likewise shāk, i.e. shawik.

It is also possible that its ʿayn is omitted, its origin being shāʾik, then the ʿayn was dropped leaving shāk, so its alif is additional and its pattern on this is fāl. As for shākin, it is a manqūṣ (defective noun), and its way is by inversion as preceded. Among the description of weapons as shākin is the saying:

2385 - وأُلْبِسُ مَنْ رضاه في طريقي ... سلاحاً يَذْعَر الأبطال شاكا
(And I clothe whoever is pleased with my way in weapons that terrify heroes, sharp.)

This may have the ʿayn omitted, or its origin may be shawik like ṣawif.

One also says: he is shākk in weapons with shaddah on the kāf, from al-shikka, which is the whole of the weapons; al-Harawī and al-Rāghib reported it.

Al-istighātha is seeking al-ghawth, which is help and aid. It was also said: al-istighātha is the filling of a lack at the time of need. It was also said: it is seeking protection. One says ghawth, ghuwāth and ghawāth; al-ghayth is of rain and al-ghawth is of help; on this, «استغاث» is shared between the two, but the difference between them is in the verb: one says istaghathtuhu, and he helped me (aghāthanī) from al-ghawth, and ghāthanī from al-ghayth. Al-irdāf is following and mounting behind you. Al-Zajjāj said: "I did ardaftu the man when I came after him." From this is {تَتْبَعُهَا الرادفة} [al-Nāziʿāt: 7], and one says radifa and ardafa. The lexicographers disagreed: it was said that they are one in meaning, which is the view of Ibn al-Aʿrābī, as Thaʿlab reported from him, and the view of Abū Zayd, as Abū ʿUbayd reported from him, who said: "One says radiftu the man and ardaftuhu when you ride behind him"; and he recited:

2386 - إذا الجوزاءُ أَرْدَفَتِ الثُّرَيَّا ... ظنَنْتُ بآل فاطمةَ الظُّنونا
(When Gemini followed the Pleiades, I thought all sorts of thoughts about the family of Fāṭima.)

i.e. it came on its heels. It was also said: rather there is a difference between them. Al-Zajjāj said: "One says radiftu the man: I rode behind him; and ardaftuhu: I made him ride behind me." This suits the view of one who supplies an object in «مُرْدِفين» with kasra on the dāl; and ardaftuhu when you come after him too, so ardafa on this becomes shared between two meanings. Shimr said: "Radiftu and ardaftu when you do that by yourself; but when you do it to someone else, ardaftu and no other."

And His saying {مُرْدَفِينَ} with fatḥa on the dāl: there are two possibilities in it. The more apparent: that it is an adjective of «أَلْف», i.e. some of them were made to ride behind others. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of those addressed in «يمدُّكم». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that by the murdafīn the believers are meant, i.e. they were followed by angels"; and this is explicit support of what I mentioned as the second possibility. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مُرْدِفين» was read with kasra on the dāl and with fatḥa, from your saying radifahu when he followed him; from it is His saying {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72], i.e. radifakum; and ardaftuhu iyyāhu when you followed him; one says ardaftuhu like ittabaʿtuhu when you came after him. The kasra'd dāl is then either in the sense of mutbiʿīn (those who cause to follow) or muttabiʿīn (those who follow). If it is in the sense of mutbiʿīn, it is either in the sense of making some of themselves follow others, or some of them making others follow, or in the sense of making the believers follow them, meaning they go before them and so make themselves follow them, or making them follow and escorting them and putting them before them while they are in their rear, so as to be under their eyes and care; or in the sense of making themselves follow other angels, or following others among the angels. This possibility is supported by His saying in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān

{بثلاثة آلافٍ من الملائكة منزلين} [Āl ʿImrān: 124] {بِخَمْسَةِ آلاف مِّنَ الملائكة مُسَوِّمِينَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 125]. And whoever read «مُرْدَفين» with fatḥa, it is in the sense of mutbaʿīn or muttabaʿīn."

I say: the explanation of this speech, for all its length, is that «أَتْبع» in its light form takes two objects, and «اتَّبع» with shaddah takes one, and ardafa has come in the sense of both, its object or two objects being omitted because the meaning is understood, so what befits each place is supplied. Except that the Shaykh faulted him for his saying "making the believers follow them" (mutbiʿīn iyyāhumu l-muʾminīn), and said: "This is not one of the places for detaching the pronoun, but of what is attached and the nūn is dropped for it; one does not say hum kāsūna iyyāka thawban, but kāsūka; so to correct it he should say mutbiʿīhimu l-muʾminīn or mutbiʿīna anfusahumu l-muʾminīn."

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا جَعَلَهُ}: the hāʾ refers to the reinforcement (imdād), i.e. "Allah did not make the reinforcement …". This reinforcement may be the one converted into a maṣdar from His saying {أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُمْ} [al-Anfāl: 9], since the meaning is: "He responded with reinforcing you." It may also be indicated by His saying «مُمِدُّكم», as its verb indicates it in His saying {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. This second is preferable because it works out on both the fatḥa and the kasra readings of «إني», unlike the first, for its referring to the reinforcement does not work on the kasra reading except by an interpretation mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī, namely that it is the object of the implied saying, so it is in the sense of the saying. It was also said that it refers to the madad (aid); al-Zajjāj said this. Al-Wāḥidī said: "This is preferable because the glad tidings was in the reinforcement with the angels." Al-Farrāʾ said: "It refers to the irdāf (following) indicated by «مردفين»." It was said: it refers to the thousand. It was said: to the promise indicated by {يَعِدُكُمُ} [al-Anfāl: 7]. It was said: to Jibrīl, or to the response (istijāba), as it is feminine figuratively, or to the announcement of the reinforcement. All are possible and the most preferable is the first; and al-jaʿl here is "making into" (taṣyīr).

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إذ يَغْشاكم}: there are several possibilities concerning «إذ». The first: it is a badal (substitute) from «إذ» in His saying {وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ} [al-Anfāl: 7]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إذ يغشاكم» is a second badal from «إذ يَعِدكم»." His saying "second" is because «إذ» in His saying «إذ تَسْتغيثون» was made a badal of it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ agreed with him on this. The second: it is accusative by «النصر» (the victory). The third: by {مِنْ عِندِ الله} [al-Anfāl: 10] on the basis of the meaning of the verb. The fourth: by {مَا جَعَلَهُ الله} [al-Anfāl: 10]. The fifth: by an implied «اذكر»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned that. Al-Ḥawfī preceded him in the fourth.

The Shaykh weakened the second possibility on three grounds. The first: it involves the governing of a maṣdar prefixed with the definite article; he said: "There is disagreement about it; the Kufans held that it does not govern." The second of the weakening grounds: it involves a separation between the maṣdar and its governed element by the predicate, which is His saying «إلا من عند الله»; and had you said «ضَرْبُ زيدٍ شديدٌ عمراً» it would not be permissible. The third: that what precedes «إلا» governs what follows it, and it is not one of the three in which that is permitted, since what precedes it does not govern what follows it unless it is the excepted, the excepted-from, or an adjective of the latter. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash allowed what precedes «إلا» to govern what follows it absolutely; and among these possibilities there is none better than that he predicated of the relative noun before the completion of its ṣila.

He weakened the third by saying that it would require the establishment of the victory to be restricted by this adverbial, whereas victory from Allah is not restricted to one time rather than another. This does not weaken it, because what is meant by this victory is a particular victory, and this particular victory was restricted to that adverbial. He weakened the fourth by the length of the separation, and that it would be governed by what precedes «إلا».

The sixth: it is accusative by His saying «ولتطمئنَّ به», al-Ṭabarī said so. The seventh: it is accusative by what «عزيز حكيم» indicates, Abū l-Baqāʾ said so, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya leaned toward it before him.

Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يَغْشاكم النعاسُ». Nāfiʿ: «يُغْشِيكم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and a light kasra'd shīn, «النعاسَ» accusative. The rest read «يُغَشِّيكم» like the one before it, except with shaddah on the shīn. The first reading is from ghashiya yaghshā, and «النعاس» is the subject. In the second it is from «أغشى», and its subject is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted; and likewise in the third, from «غَشَّى» with shaddah. «النعاس» in both is the direct object; and aghshā and ghashshā are two dialectal forms.

His saying «أَمَنَةً»: there are three [possibilities] for its being accusative. The first: it is a maṣdar of an implied verb, i.e. "so you felt secure, security". The second: it is accusative as standing in the place of a ḥāl: either from the subject — if the subject is «النعاس», then attributing security to it is figurative; if it is the Creator, the Exalted, as in the last two readings, the attribution is literal — or from the object, by hyperbole, i.e. making them the very self of security, or on an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of security".

The third: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and that is either on the last two readings or on the first. On the last two readings its matter is clear: the covering or the causing to be covered is from Allah the Exalted, and the security is also from Him, so the agent is the same and the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi is sound. As for the first reading, the subject of «يغشى» is the drowsiness and the subject of «الأمنة» is the Creator, the Exalted. With the difference of agent, the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi is prevented according to the well-known view, though there is disagreement in it, unless it is allowed by figurative licence.

Al-Zamakhsharī made that clear, saying: "«وأَمَنَةً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. If you say: is it not obligatory that the agent of the verb and of the reason be one? I say: yes, but since the meaning of «يَغْشاكم النعاسُ» is 'you doze', «أَمَنَةً» is accusative in the sense that the drowsiness and the security are theirs, and the meaning is: when you dozed in security." Then he said: "If you say: may it be accusative on the basis that the security belongs to the drowsiness that overwhelms you, i.e. 'drowsiness overwhelms you for the sake of security', the attribution of security to the drowsiness being a figurative attribution and for the possessors of drowsiness literally; or on the basis that it came to you at a time when it was proper for drowsiness, in that fearful time, not to precede its overwhelming you, and it overwhelmed you only because of a security obtained for it from Allah, without which it would not have overwhelmed you, in the manner of representation and imagery." I say: the eloquence of the Quran is not far from such a thing, and it has parallels, and the one who said this has hinted at it:

2387 - يَهاب النَّوْمُ أن يَغْشى عيوناً ... تهابُكَ فهْوَ نَفَّارٌ شَرودُ
(Sleep fears to overwhelm eyes that fear you, so it is shy and fleeing.)

And His saying {مِنْه} is accusative in position as an adjective of «أَمَنَة»; the pronoun in «منه» may refer to the Creator, the Exalted, or to the drowsiness by the figurative usage mentioned above.

Ibn Muḥayṣin, al-Nakhaʿī and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «أَمْنَةً» with sukūn on the mīm. The parallel of amina amanatan with vowelled mīm is ḥayiya ḥayātan, and the parallel of amina amnatan with sukūn is raḥima raḥmatan.

His saying {مَآءً لِّيُطَهِّرَكُمْ}: the majority read «ماءً» with the long form. «ليطهركم» is attached to «يُنَزِّل». Al-Shaʿbī read «ما ليطهركم» with a short alif, and there are two derivations in it. The more apparent, which Ibn Jinnī and others mentioned, is that «ما» is in the sense of «الذي» and «ليطهِّرَكم» is its ṣila; some said its implied form is «الذي هو ليطهركم», supplying the prepositional phrase as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the clause being the ṣila of «ما». The Shaykh rejected these two derivations, because the lām of «kay» (purpose) does not occur as a ṣila. The second: that «ما» is «ماء» with the long form, but the Arabs have dropped its hamza and said «شربت ماً» with a tanwīn'd mīm, as Ibn Miqsam reported; and this has no parallel, since it is not permissible to violate a declinable noun by omission until it remains on one letter.

If that is known, it is possible that he shortened it, and did not give it tanwīn because he treated continuation as pause. Then this alif may be the middle letter of the word, with the hamza omitted, this alif being a substitute for the wāw which is in «مَوَهَ» originally; or it may be the one substituted for the tanwīn, treating continuation as pause. The first is preferable because they take care in pause not to leave the thing paused upon with only one letter, such as «مُرٍ», the active participle of arā yurī.

His saying «ويُذْهِبَ» is a coordination (nasaq) upon «ليطهِّركم». ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «ويُذْهِبْ» with sukūn on the bāʾ, which is a lightening that the Shaykh called a jussive. The majority read «رِجز» with kasra on the rāʾ and the zāy. Ibn Muḥayṣin read with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla with the sīn. Discussion of each of these has preceded. The meaning of «رجز الشيطان» here is what arises from his whispering.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ يُوحِي}: there are several possibilities in it. The first: it is a third badal (substitute) from His saying {وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ} [al-Anfāl: 7]. The second: that it is accusative by His saying «ويثبِّتَ»; al-Zamakhsharī said both and did not build that on the return of the pronoun. As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya, he built it on the return of the pronoun in His saying «به», saying: "The governor in «إذ» is the first governor, as preceded concerning what is before it; and had we supplied it as near, His saying «ويُثَبِّتَ» would be on the interpretation of its referring to the binding; but on the interpretation of its referring to the water, it is awkward that «ويثبت» govern «إذ»." It is awkward to him because of the difference between the time of the strengthening and the time of the revelation: for the sending down of rain and the explanations connected with it precede the covering with drowsiness, whereas this revelation, the covering with drowsiness and the inspiration were at the time of fighting.

His saying: {أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ}: an object of «يوحي», i.e. "He inspires that I am with you with victory and triumph." ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, with a disagreement from him, read «إني معكم» with kasra on the hamza. There are two possibilities in it. The first: that this is on the implication of a saying, which is the school of the Basrans. The second: treating «يوحي» as the saying because it is in its meaning, which is the school of the Kufans. His saying: {فَوْقَ الأعناق}: there are several possibilities in it. The first: «فوق» remains an adverb, and the object is omitted, i.e. "strike them above the necks"; He taught them how to strike them. The second: «فوق» is a direct object by extension, since it stands for the head, as if it were said: "strike their heads." This is not good, because it is not declined. Some claimed that it is declined and that you say «فوقُك رأسُك» with «فوقك» nominative, and this is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's saying, for he said: "«فوق الأعناق»: he meant the tops of the necks, which are the slaughtering places, which are joints." The third, and it is the view of Abū ʿUbayda: it is in the sense of «على», i.e. "on the necks", the object being omitted, its implied form: "strike them on the necks", and it is close to the first. The fourth: Ibn Qutayba said: "It is in the sense of «دون»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is a plain error and a gross mistake; what confused him was only His saying {بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا} [al-Baqara: 26], i.e. 'what is below it', and «فوق» here is not in the sense of «دون»; what is meant is rather: 'what is above it in smallness and littleness'." The fifth: that it is redundant, i.e. "strike the necks", which is the view of Abū l-Ḥasan; and according to the majority this is an error, because adding nouns redundantly is not permitted.

His saying: {مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ}: «منهم» may be attached to the command before it, i.e. "begin the striking from these places and limbs, from their upper parts to their lower." It may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «كلَّ بنان»; because originally it could be an adjective of it had it come later. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak that it be a ḥāl from «بنان», since it involves fronting the ḥāl of the muḍāf ilayhi before the muḍāf." So the meaning would be: "strike them in whatever way."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He means striking the head," and said:

2388 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأَضْرِبُ هامةَ البطلِ المُشيحِ
(… and I strike the head of the determined hero.)

And he said:

2389 - غَشَّيْتُه وَهْو في جَأْواءَ باسلةٍ ... عَضْباً أصابَ سَواءَ الرأسِ فانفلقا
(I covered him, while he was in a grim, fierce army, with a sharp sword that hit the middle of the head and split it.)

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that by His saying «فوق الأعناق» he intends to describe the most effective of the blows to the neck, which is the blow that comes above the bone of the neck and below the bone of the head," then he said: "From it is his saying:

2390 - جَعَلْتُ السيفَ بين الجِيْدِ مِنْه ... وبين أَسِيْلِ خَدَّيْه عِذارا"
(I put the sword between his neck and his smooth cheeks as a chin-strap.)

It was also said: this is mentioning the part and intending the whole, like the saying of ʿAntara:

2391 - عَهْدي به شَدَّ النهار كأنما ... خُضِب البَنانُ ورأسُه بالعِظْلم
(My last knowledge of him was at the height of day, as if his fingertips and head were dyed with indigo.)

Al-banān: it was said to be the fingers, and it is a generic noun, the singular being banāna. ʿAntara said:

2392 - وإنَّ الموتَ طَوْعُ يدي إذا ما ... وصلْتُ بنانَها بالهُنْدُواني
(Death is at my hand's command, when I join its fingers with the Indian blade.)

Abū l-Haytham said: "Al-banān: the joints, and every joint is a banāna." It was said: al-banān is the fingers of the hands and feet. It was said: the fingers of the hands and feet and all joints of all limbs; and he recited for ʿAntara:

2393 - وكان فتى الهَيْجاءِ يَحْمي ذِمارَها ... ويَضْرِبُ عند الكَرْب كلَّ بنانِ
(He was the youth of battle, protecting its honour, and in distress striking every finger-tip.)

Its final nūn may be replaced by a mīm. Ruʾba said:

2394 - يا هالَ ذاتَ المَنْطِقِ النَّمْنامِ ... وكَفِّك المخضَّبِ البنَامِ
(O Hāl, of the dainty speech, and your hand with the dyed fingertips.)

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذلك بِأَنَّهُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar? The reference is to the command to strike them, and the address may be to the Messenger, or may be to the disbelievers, in which case it would be an iltifāt (shift of person). Thus said the Shaykh, and there is room for objection in it for two reasons. The first: it would require addressing a plural with the address of the singular, which is either prohibited or rare, though a minor dialectal form has been reported. The second: after it comes «بأنهم شاقُّوا», so he would have shifted from the third person to the address in a single word, then returned to the third person immediately, which is remote.

His saying: {وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ الله}: «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause after it is its khabar, or the clause occurring as the apodosis, or the two together. Whoever insists that a pronoun from the clause of the apodosis return to the conditional noun supplies it here as omitted, its implied form being: "then Allah is severe in punishment for him." The readers agreed on the unassimilated form here in «يُشاقِق», because the muṣḥafs wrote it with two unassimilated qāfs; and the unassimilated form of this kind is the dialect of the Hijaz, while assimilation, with its conditions, is the dialect of Tamīm.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذلكم فَذُوقُوهُ}: four possibilities are allowed for «ذلكم». The first: it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the punishment is that" or "the matter is that". The second: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e. "that is the punishment". On these two possibilities, His saying «فذوقوه» has no grammatical connection with what precedes it. The third: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is His saying «فذوقوه»; this is according to al-Akhfash, who holds the fāʾ to be redundant (zāʾida) absolutely, I mean whether or not the mubtadaʾ contains the sense of a condition; others do not allow its redundancy except on the condition that the mubtadaʾ resembles a conditional noun, and I have set out its exposition more than once. Al-Akhfash cited as evidence for the permissibility of that the poet's saying:

2395 - وقائلةٍ خولانُ فانكِحْ فتاتَهُمْ ... وأُكْرومَةُ الحَيَّيْنِ خِلْوٌ كما هيا
(Many a woman says: "Khawlān — so marry their girl", while the noble one of the two tribes is single as she is.)

The others derived it on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "this is Khawlān". The fourth: it is accusative by an implied verb which what follows explains, belonging to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be accusative on the basis of «عليكم ذلكم», as in: «زيداً فاضربه»." The Shaykh said: "This supposition is not sound, because «عليكم» is among the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl), and verbal nouns are not implied; so his likening it to your saying «زيداً فاضرِبْه» is not good, because they did not supply it as «عليك زيداً فاضربه»; rather this is accusative by ishtighāl." I say: it is possible that al-Zamakhsharī leaned toward the Kufans, who treat it as a verb absolutely, and likewise make it govern when delayed, such as {كِتَابَ الله عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 24].

Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be in the accusative position, i.e. 'taste that', the verb after it being made to explain it; and the better is that the implied form be 'undertake that, so taste it', so that the fāʾ is a conjunction." I say: the apparent sense of this second statement is that the matter is not one of ishtighāl, because he supplied a verb not agreeing in wording with what follows although that was possible; and also he made the fāʾ a conjunction and not redundant. The investigation of the discussion of this fāʾ has preceded at His saying {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون} [al-Baqara: 40].

His saying: {وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ النار}: the majority read «أنَّ» with fatḥa, and there are several derivations. The first: that it and what is in its scope are in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar omitted, its implied form: "the establishment of the punishment of the Fire for the disbelievers is decreed". The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the decree" or "the obligatory thing is that for the disbelievers", or "the obligatory thing is that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire". The third: that it is conjoined to «ذلكم» in its two possibilities, as al-Zamakhsharī said, and by "in its two possibilities" he means the two nominative possibilities, which have preceded. The fourth: that it is in the accusative position as accompaniment; al-Zamakhsharī said: "or accusative on the basis that the wāw means 'with', the meaning being: taste this immediate punishment together with the deferred one that is yours in the Hereafter, putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun." By "putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun" he means that the original wording is «فذوقوه وأن لكم», so he put «للكافرين» in the place of «لكم», as testimony against them of disbelief and a pointer to the cause. The fifth: that it is in the accusative position by an implied «اعلموا» (know). The poet said:

2396 - تسمع للأَحْشاء منه لَغَطَاً ... ولليدين جُسْأَةً وبَدَدا
(You hear from its entrails a rumbling, and for the two hands a hardness and a spreading apart.)

i.e. "and you see in the two hands a spreading apart", so he implied «ترى»; likewise «فذوقوه: واعلموا أنَّ للكافرين». Al-Zajjāj denied it most strongly and said: "Had this been permissible, it would be permissible: «زيد قائم وعمراً منطلقاً», i.e. 'and you see ʿAmr departing', and no one permits it."

Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, as resumptive.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {زَحْفاً}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: it is accusative as a maṣdar, and its governor is in the accusative position as a ḥāl, the implied form being: "when you meet those who disbelieve, advancing, an advance", or "they advance, an advance". The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl by itself. Then they differed regarding the owner of the ḥāl: it was said to be the subject, i.e. "while you are a zaḥf among the zuḥūf", i.e. a mass; or "while you are walking toward them little by little", according to how zaḥf is explained, and it will come. It was said: it is the object, i.e. "while they are a great multitude" or "walking toward you". It was said: it is a ḥāl from both, i.e. "you met them advancing, some of you toward others".

Al-zaḥf is drawing near little by little; one says zaḥafa yazḥafu ilayhi, with fatḥa in both, so he is zāḥif, zaḥfan; and likewise tazaḥḥafa, tazāḥafa; and azḥafa lanā ʿaduwwunā, i.e. they drew near to fight us. Al-Layth said: "Al-zaḥf is a group walking toward their enemy; al-Aʿshā said:

2397 - لِمَنِ الظعائنُ سَيَّرُهُنَّ تَزَحُّفُ ... مثلَ السَّفِينِ إذا تقاذَفُ تَجْدِفُ
(Whose are the howdah-camels whose journey is a crawling advance, like ships, when they are tossed, rowing?)

This belongs to the chapter of applying the maṣdar to a concrete thing. Al-zaḥf is also creeping, from «زَحَفَ الصبيُّ» (the child crawled); Imruʾ al-Qays said:

2398 - فَزَحْفاً أَتَيْتُ على الرُّكْبَتَيْنِ ... فثوباً لَبِسْتُ وثوباً أَجُرّْ
(So I came crawling on my knees; one garment I wore, and one I dragged.)

It may be pluralised as zuḥūf and mazāḥif, because of the difference of kind. The Hudhalī said:

2399 - كأنَّ مَزاحِفَ الحَيَّاتِ فيه ... قبيل الصُّبْحِ آثارُ السِّياطِ
(As if the trails of the snakes in it, just before dawn, were the marks of whips.)

And mazāḥif is the plural of mazḥaf, an ism maṣdar.

His saying: «الأَدْبار» is the object of «تُوَلُّوهم».

semin-durr:16-16.t:
Likewise {دُبُرَه} is the second object of {يُوَلِّهم}. Al-Ḥasan read it with sukūn, like their saying ʿunq for ʿunuq. This belongs to the chapter of allusion (taʿrīḍ), in that He mentioned for them a state that is held disgraceful in its doer, so He used the word al-dubur rather than al-ẓahr for that reason. Some of the people of the science of rhetoric called this kind kināya (metonymy), and that is nothing.

His saying: {إلا مُتَحرِّفاً}: there are two possibilities for its being accusative. The first: that it is a ḥāl. The second: that it is an exception. Al-Zamakhsharī made that clear, saying: "If you say: by what is «إلا متحرِّفاً» accusative? I say: as a ḥāl, «إلا» being laghw (otiose); or as an exception from those who turn their backs, i.e. 'whoever turns his back to them, except a man among them manoeuvring or joining'." The Shaykh said: "By his saying 'إلا is laghw' he does not mean that it is redundant, but that the governor, which is «يُوَلِّهم», reaches what follows it, as they say in «جئت بلا زاد» that it is laghw; and in reality it is an exception from an omitted ḥāl, the implied form being: 'whoever turns his back to them in whatever state, except in such and such a state'; and if a general omitted ḥāl is not supplied, the entry of «إلا» would not be sound, because the condition in their view is affirmative, and the ruling on the affirmative is that «إلا» does not enter into it, neither in the object nor in other complements, because it would be an incomplete exception (mufarragh), and the incomplete exception occurs only with negation or prohibition, or what is interpreted as them; and if there comes what is apparently contrary to that, it is interpreted." I say: his saying "neither in the object nor in other complements" is unnecessary, because the incomplete exception does not enter an affirmation absolutely, whether what is after «إلا» is a complement or a mainstay; so mentioning the complement and the object suggests its permissibility in others.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "As for the exception, it is from the ones who turn their backs whom «مَنْ» includes." So he made its accusative as an exception. A group said: the exception is from the kinds of turning the back. This has been rejected, since if it were so the construction would have to be «إلا تحيُّزاً أو تحرُّفاً».

Al-taḥayyuz and al-tajawwuz: joining. Taḥawwazat al-ḥayya: the snake coiled; ḥuztu l-shayʾa: I enclosed the thing. Al-ḥawza is what gathers things together. The pattern of mutaḥayyiz is mutafayʿil, the origin being mutaḥaywiz. The yāʾ and the wāw met, with the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was turned into yāʾ and assimilated into the yāʾ after it, like mayyit. It cannot be mutafaʿʿil, for were it so, it would be mutaḥawwiz; as for mutaḥawwiz, it is mutafaʿʿil.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ}: there are two possibilities for this fāʾ. The first, which al-Zamakhsharī held: that it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you boast of killing them, you did not kill them." The Shaykh said: "It is not an apodosis but to link the speech one part with another."

His saying: {ولكن الله قَتَلَهُمْ}: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ibn ʿĀmir read «ولكن الله قَتَلهم» and «ولكن الله رمى» with the light «لكن» and the divine name nominative; the rest with the doubled one and the divine name accusative. The justification of the two readings has been given fully at His saying {ولكن الشياطين} [al-Baqara: 104]. «لكن» came here in the finest way, as it occurs between negation and affirmation; and His saying {وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ} negated the throwing from him and affirmed it for him, and that from two considerations: i.e. "you did not throw in reality when you threw in outward appearance", or "you did not throw terror into their hearts when you threw pebbles and dust." His saying «وما رَمَيْتَ» is a clause conjoined to His saying «فلم تقتلوهم», because the imperfect negated by «لم» has the force of the past negated by «ما»; for when you say «لم يَقُم», its meaning is «ما قام». And He did not say here "you did not kill them when you killed them", as He said «إذ رَمَيْت», as hyperbole in the second clause.

His saying: {وَلِيُبْلِيَ المؤمنين} is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "and He did that so that He might test". Or it is conjoined to an omitted cause, i.e. "but Allah threw so as to wipe out the disbelievers and so as to test the believers." Al-balāʾ occurs in good and in evil. Zuhayr said:

2400 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأبلاهما خيرَ البلاء الذي يبلو
(… and He tried the two of them with the best of the trial with which He tries.)

The hāʾ in «منه» refers to the triumph over the polytheists. It was said: to the throwing; Makkī said both. The apparent sense is that it refers to Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذلكم}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ is permissible, i.e. "that is the matter", with the khabar omitted, as al-Ḥawfī said; and the better is that the khabar be supplied as "that trial is true and decreed". It was also said: it is the khabar of a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that", which is Sībawayh's supposition. It was said: its position is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "He did that". The reference in «ذلكم» is to the killing, the throwing and the testing. His saying «بلاءً» may be an ism maṣdar, i.e. ibtilāʾ; and it may be that by al-balāʾ the very thing with which one is tested is meant.

His saying: {وَأَنَّ الله}: it may be conjoined to «ذلكم», so its position is judged as the position of «ذلكم» is judged, as has preceded; and it may be in the accusative position by an implied verb, i.e. "and know that Allah", and what is in that has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is conjoined to «وليُبْلي»," meaning that the purpose is the testing of the believers and the weakening of the plot of the disbelievers.

Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read «مُوْهِن» with sukūn on the wāw and a light hāʾ, from awhana like akrama. Everyone except Ḥafṣ gave «موهن» tanwīn. The rest read «مُوَهِّن» with fatḥa on the wāw, shaddah on the hāʾ and tanwīn. So «كيد» is accusative as a direct object in the reading of everyone except Ḥafṣ, and genitive in Ḥafṣ's reading, its origin being accusative. The Kufans' reading came on the more frequent pattern, because a verb whose middle letter is a guttural other than the hamza is made transitive by the hamza, and is not made transitive by doubling except a few memorised words such as wahhantuhu and ḍaʿʿaftuhu.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَن تُغْنِيَ}: the majority read with the upper tāʾ (tughniya), because al-fiʾa (the troop) is feminine. «ولن يُغْني» was also read with the lower tāʾ (yaghniya), because its feminine is figurative and also because of the separation. «ولو كَثُرَت»: this clause of impossibility (imtināʿiyya) is a ḥāl, and its investigation has preceded.

His saying: {وَأَنَّ الله مَعَ المؤمنين}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read with fatḥa, and the rest with kasra. The fatḥa has several possibilities. The first: that it is on the lām of reason, the implied form being: "and because Allah is with the believers, such and such happened." The second: that the implied form is: "and because Allah is with the believers, their stubbornness was prevented." The third: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and the matter is that Allah is with the believers." This last possibility is close in meaning to the kasra reading, because it is resumptive.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَوَلَّوْا}: the original is «تَتَوَلَّوا», and one of the two tāʾs was dropped. The disagreement about which of them is dropped has preceded.

His saying: {وَأَنْتُمْ تَسْمَعُونَ} is a ḥāl clause, and the pronoun in «عنه» refers to the Messenger, because obeying him is part of obeying Allah. It was said: it refers to Allah, and this is like His saying, the Exalted, {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62]. It was said: it refers to the command to obey.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {الصم}: «الصُمُّ», which is the khabar of «شر», was pluralised only because plurality is meant by it, so the khabar was pluralised according to the meaning; had it been «الأصم», the singular would have followed the wording; so the meaning is plural.

And His saying: {الذين لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ} may be nominative or accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment).

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بَيْنَ المرء}: the majority read the mīm with fatḥa; Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with kasra, as a following of the vowel of the hamza. That is because «المَرْء» has two dialectal forms, the more eloquent being fatḥa on the mīm absolutely; and the second, by making the mīm follow the vowel of the case, so you say «هذا مُرْءٌ» with ḍamma on the mīm, «رأيت مَرْءاً» with fatḥa, and «مررت بمِرْءٍ» with kasra. Al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī read it with fatḥa on the mīm and shaddah on the rāʾ. Its justification is that he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the rāʾ, then doubled the rāʾ, treating continuation as pause.

His saying: «وأنه»: the hāʾ may be the pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), and it may refer to Allah the Exalted, which is the better in view of «الله».

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ}: there are two possibilities for «لا». The first: that it is prohibitive (nāhiya); on this the clause cannot be an adjective of «فتنة», since an imperative-type (ṭalabī) clause does not occur as an adjective; it may be governed by an implied saying, that saying being the adjective, i.e. "a trial about which it is said: let it not befall…". The prohibition is in form addressed to the affliction and in meaning to those addressed, and it is in meaning like their saying «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» (let me not see you here), i.e. "do not engage in causes by which an affliction will strike you that does not single out the wrongdoer among you." The nūn of emphasis on this view is in its place. The parallel of implying a saying is the saying:

2401 - جاؤوا بمَذْقٍ هل رأيتَ الذئبَ قَطْ ... أي: مقول فيه: هل رأيت
(They came with diluted milk — "have you ever seen the wolf?" — i.e. one about which it is said: have you seen.)

The second: that «لا» is negative, and the clause is an adjective of «فتنة»; this is clear from this angle, except that the emphasis of the imperfect in other than an oath, request or condition is problematic for it, and there is disagreement in it: whether negation with «لا» runs in the course of prohibition. Some people said yes, and cited the saying:

2402 - فلا الجارةُ الدنيا لها تَلْحَيَنَّها ... ولا الضيفُ منها إنْ أناخَ مُحَوَّلُ
(The near neighbour-woman — you will not blame her; nor is the guest, if he camps, moved on from her.)

Another said:

2403 - فلا ذا نعيمٍ يُتْرَكَنْ لنعيمه ... وإن قال قَرِّظْني وخُذْ رشوةً أبى
ولا ذا بيئسٍ يُتركنَّ لبؤسه ... فينفعَه شكوٌ إليه إن اشْتكى
(No possessor of ease is left to his ease, even if he says "praise me and take a bribe", he refuses; and no possessor of misery is left to his misery, such that a complaint to him would benefit him if he complained.)

So if it is permissible to emphasise what is negated by «لا» with a separation, then it is a fortiori permissible to emphasise what is negated without separation. Except that the majority take that as poetic necessity.

Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «لا تصيبَنَّ» is an answer to the imperative, as in «انزلْ عن الدابة لا تَطْرَحَنَّك», i.e. "if you get off it, it will not throw you"; and from it His saying {لاَ يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ} [al-Naml: 18], i.e. "if you enter, they will not crush you"; and the nūn entered because of the sense of requital in it. The Shaykh said: "His saying «لا يَحْطِمَنَّكم»: this example is not a parallel of «فتنةً لا تصيبنَّ الذين», because from the verse and the example a condition and requital are formed as he supposed, and that is not formed here; do you not see that the supposition 'if you guard against a trial, it will not befall those who did wrong' is not sound, since there follows from the condition something other than what it requires in meaning."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«لا تصيبنَّ»: it is either an answer to an imperative, or a prohibition after a command, or an adjective of «فتنة». If it is an answer, the meaning is: if it befalls you, it will not befall only the wrongdoers among you, but will embrace you all." The Shaykh said: "Al-Zamakhsharī took al-Farrāʾ's view and increased its corruption and muddled it," mentioning what I have transmitted from him, then said: "Look at him: how he supposed that it is an answer to the imperative, which is «اتقوا», then supposed the conditional particle to enter upon other than the imperfect of «اتقوا», for he said: the meaning is 'if it befalls you', meaning the trial. And look how al-Farrāʾ supposed: 'get off the animal, it will not throw you', and in His saying

{ادخلوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ لاَ يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ} [al-Naml: 18], so he put a conditional particle before the imperfect of the imperative verb, and so [is supplied] whatever is an answer to an imperative."

It was also said: «لا تصيبنَّ» is the answer to an omitted oath, and the oath clause is an adjective of «فتنة», i.e. "a trial, by Allah, will not befall". The entry of the nūn is also rare because it is negated. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The nūn entered the negated verb, outside an oath, irregularly," and the apparent sense of this is that when the negation is in the answer of an oath, the entry of the nūn is regular; and it is not so.

It was also said: the lām is the lām of emphasis, and the verb after it is affirmative, only the lām was lengthened, i.e. its fatḥa was extended, producing an alif; so the entry of the nūn in it is regular. This speaker was influenced by the reading of a large group, «لتصيبَنَّ», which is the reading of the Commander of the Believers, Ibn Masʿūd, Zayd ibn Thābit, al-Bāqir, al-Rabīʿ, Anas, Abū l-ʿĀliya and Ibn Jammāz. Among those who justified it is Ibn Jinnī. The wonder is that he justified this irregular reading with a justification that returns it to the majority reading, saying: "It is possible that the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and those mentioned with him is a lightened form of «لا», meaning the alif of «لا» was dropped for lightness and the vowel sufficed", saying: "as they said «أمَ والله» meaning «أما والله»." Al-Mahdawī said: "as it is dropped from «ما», which is the sister of «لا», in «أما والله لأفعلنَّ» and its like." His saying "the sister of «لا»" is not so, because this «أما» is for opening speech like «ألا», and is nothing of the negative. It follows from this that Ibn Jinnī derived each of the two readings from the other, and this ought not to be permitted at all: how can one bring a word of negation and interpret it as affirmation, and the reverse? This only inverts realities and leads to obscurity.

Al-Mubarrad, al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said regarding the majority reading «لا تصيبنَّ»: "The speech was complete at His saying «فتنة», and it is a general address to the believers; then He began the prohibition of the wrongdoers in particular from drawing near to wrongdoing, so that the trial strikes them in particular. What is meant here is: let not the wrongdoer expose himself to the trial so that its striking falls on him in particular."

Al-Zamakhsharī said in establishing this possibility: "If it is a prohibition after a command, it is as if it were said: 'Beware of a sin or a punishment', then it is said: 'Do not expose yourselves to wrongdoing, so that the punishment or the effect of the sin strikes those among you who did wrong, in particular.'"

ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: "It is a prohibition in the sense of supplication. He made it a prohibition in the sense of supplication only because the entry of the nūn into what is negated with «لا» is not permitted in his view; so the meaning becomes: 'may it not strike a wrongdoer or a non-wrongdoer', as if it were said: 'and guard against a trial that Allah does not bring upon anyone.'" I have gathered from the preceding, in the derivation of this word, several views: prohibition with its two suppositions, supplication with its two suppositions, answer to the imperative with its two suppositions, and its being an adjective with the supposition of a saying.

His saying: {مِنْكُمْ}: there are three possibilities in it, the most apparent being that it is explanatory (bayān) absolutely. The second: that it is a ḥāl and so is attached to an omitted element. Al-Zamakhsharī made it partitive (tabʿīḍ) on one supposition and explanatory on another, saying: "If you say: what is the meaning of «مِن» in His saying «الذين ظلموا منكم»? I say: partition on the first possibility and explanation on the second; because the meaning is: 'it will strike you in particular for your wrongdoing, because wrongdoing from you is uglier than from the rest of the people.'" I say: he means by the first its being an answer to a command, and by the second its being a prohibition after a command. In his restricting partition to one of the two possibilities and not the other, and likewise the second, there is room for objection, since the meaning is sound on either supposition with both partition and explanation.

His saying: {خَاصَّةً}: there are three possibilities in it. The first, and it is the apparent one: it is a ḥāl from the latent subject in His saying «لا تصيبنَّ», and its origin is that it be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being "a striking particular (iṣāba khāṣṣa)". The second: that it is a ḥāl from the object, which is the relative noun, the implied form being: "it will not strike the wrongdoers in particular, but will embrace them and others". The third: that it is a ḥāl from the subject of «ظلموا», as Ibn ʿAṭiyya said. The Shaykh said: "This possibility is not intelligible." I say: I do not know what its unintelligibility is. For the meaning is: "guard against a trial that will not strike those who did wrong while others did not do wrong", in the sense that they were singled out for wrongdoing and no one else shared it with them; so this trial does not confine its striking to these people themselves, and it strikes those who did not do wrong at all; and this is a clear meaning.
